Then, if a soldier makes his pay his own, and his wage his own, why would the revenues assigned to a cleric as his stipend not become his own? He also adduces custom: for in Spain there is a custom, whose origin exceeds memory, by which clerics who are not bishops are permitted, in life and in death, to dispose of the fruits of their benefices, and their heirs on intestacy succeed them if they die intestate, whereas bishops dispose only during life; Colonna adds this, c. 36, and this is the case in France too. The same opinion is followed by Antonio Marsilio Colonna, in his de Ecclesiasticorum redituum origine, part 3, c. 21, who in the same place does not want that argument to proceed as it is commonly taken, from the non-ownership of clerics to the obligation of restitution; and so the questions whether beneficed clerics are owners of ecclesiastical revenues, and whether, if they consume them badly, they are bound to restitution, should not be confused. Moreover, in c. 26 he brings forward other reasons for Thomas's opinion (which in c. last he also teaches: that clerics not only make themselves owners of their goods or ecclesiastical revenues, but also free themselves from every burden of restitution), after in the preceding c. 25 he had largely answered the reasons brought by Sarmiento. Yet in c. 33 he adds this limitation to Thomas's opinion: that although a cleric is not bound to restitution, or even if he grossly abuses the goods of the Church, yet this does not hold when he has altogether deserted his office. He counts up fifty-five doctors as supporters of his opinion, and thirty-four on the opposing side, that of the Archdeacon (cc. 34 and 35). Sarmiento in brief, in the preface to Pope Pius V, had begged him to determine, by his apostolic authority, what men are bound to by precept, and what it would be expedient to follow by counsel here. But so far (as far as I know) the Pope has not done so, nor does he try to do so in most disputes of this kind, however fiercely they are carried on among his own people. This is surely remarkable, since he asserts both that the judgment of theological questions is infallible in his own hands, and that all laws are kept in the coffer of his breast; and finally, since he wishes to be approached as judge, among others who are alien to his communion, and in matters far weightier, when he will not, or cannot, settle those waves in his own house. But let us get on. We know that even the Gentiles observed this with religious care: they carried out the last wills of testators, and did not allow anyone to violate what had at some time been consecrated to God, or to turn it to their own uses. Pythagoras is said to have signified this by that symbol of his: "Do not heap up cypress wood," that is, goods consecrated to God, since the sceptre of Jupiter was made of cypress. Pisistratus, in Laertius's Life of Solon, writes thus: "Finally, each of the Athenians sets aside the tithes of his produce, not to be consumed for our uses, but for public sacrifices and common needs; and whenever war comes upon us, they are to be applied to the expenses." From the Laws of the Twelve Tables: "Whoever steals what is sacred, or what has been entrusted to a sacred use, shall be condemned to death." Rogerius, who recently wrote or published the history of the present-day Brachmans, or Brahmins, about their life, teaching and customs, says that neither the King nor anyone dares to take away from the Brahmins a field or farm given to them, because they fear the grave vengeance of their god, should they ever try to take what belongs to poor Brahmins (bk. 1, ch. 6). Something of this sort, they say, happened to their King Rama Dewelo and his minister, when they attempted to carry off certain treasures from the buildings of the pagodas (bk. 2, ch. 10). Add Valerius Maximus, bk. 1, ch. 1. While we are not ignorant of these things, they bid us abstain from violating ecclesiastical goods, that is, those things given and donated to God for His worship and for the ministry of the Church; and they release us all the more strongly from that reproach which the Pope vainly casts at us, as if we took away the goods of the churches and did not teach that they are to be spent on ecclesiastical uses. That it is otherwise, I think can already be sufficiently clear to anyone from what we have brought forward. v. Indeed, long ago in the Treaty of Passau, by imperial authority, ecclesiastical goods were granted to the Protestants: whatever our people then possessed, however much had been derived from the Papists and seized by them, and which they applied to ecclesiastical uses. And before the Treaty of Passau, at the Diet of Hagenau in 1540, in reply to the Papists' objection concerning ecclesiastical goods taken away and diverted by our people to other uses, they answered: that they had seized no one's goods; only after the doctrine of their purity had been restored to its gold, had they applied again to lawful and honourable uses the goods which had originally been destined for them, but had afterwards been diverted from ecclesiastical ones; and therefore that the heads of doctrine were to be settled first, and the question of goods was to be discussed afterwards. So it is in the History of the Council of Trent, bk. 1. And in Sleidan, bk. 13: "But they say that no one has been despoiled by them, and that this very question belongs to the colloquy and the future proceedings; and that sequestration cannot be made without great dissipation of their ecclesiastical polity, and to the detriment of the schools and of the poor. And since the day of the colloquy is not far off, they ask that the whole matter be deferred to it: there they will show how much more they labour and are anxious for the glory of God, and for the reform of the churches, than for possessions and goods; and although they can already show how some of the opposite party snatch such resources to themselves, yet they want those to be put off; and when the matter is discussed, it will be clear which party turns those possessions more to their own private advantage than to the honour of God, and what hinders their being applied to better uses." What, then, is the Pope now moving, anew, about those goods adjudged and claimed for our side? Especially since that peace was confirmed again, both by the Treaty of Passau and by this recent Peace of Osnabrück, art. 5. The decree, made in the Assembly first at Linz and soon after at Passau, on 11 August 1552, is that the peace of religion, whether or not the controversy is settled, shall be ratified and firm. And finally, in the Diet of Augsburg on 25 September 1555, that Treaty of Passau was confirmed, and it was established that ecclesiastical goods which were not states of the Empire, or did not belong to them, and which our people had occupied before the transaction at Passau and had transferred to pious uses, should not be claimed again either in court or out of court, nor could our people on that account be sued. Sleidan, Commentaries, bk. 26; Thuanus, History, bk. 16. Anyone who understands this otherwise is not sufficiently skilled in these matters: the meaning is that when the peace of religion was made at Augsburg in 1555, it was agreed between the Emperor and the Protestant princes of the Empire that ecclesiastical goods occupied by them should be turned to pious uses. For the words, that they should remain in the state in which they then were, mean that those things which they already held would remain with the Protestants, and were not to be yielded to the Papists; and that, as they had also been applied to sacred uses among the Protestants, which they certainly were unwilling to oppose in any way. As for the Papists, what they said was that those goods had not been applied to sacred uses by the Protestants with sufficient good faith, and so, as if the conditions of the Treaty of Passau had not been kept, they could safely be claimed back from them. For the holders of ecclesiastical goods argued thus from the articles of the treaty, that they are to be counted as such even in the external forum, and must be compelled to restitution.

units.la: 1. Qui non sunt Status Imperii, hoc est, non habent sessionem in publicis Imperii Comitiis. 2. Qui occuparunt post terminum admissum, hoc est, 2. Augusti, Anni 1552. 3. Qui occuparunt Bona, quae sunt Status Imperii, vel ad eosdem spectant, uti sunt omnes Episcopatus, Abbatiae & Praeturae, quae in matricula Imperii extant. 4. Qui transtulerunt ad alios usus quam pios. Visus autem pius censetur applicatio ad pauperes, Ecclesias, & Scholas in Imperio admissas (Catholicas scilicet, vel Augustanae Confessionis, exclusis omnibus aliis) redemptionem captivorum, & similes. Sic. illi Ipsa autem Comitiorum verba nos hic exhibeamus
units.tr: 1. Those who are not Estates of the Empire, that is, who do not have a seat at the public Imperial Diets. 2. Those who took possession after the cut-off date fixed, that is, 2 August 1552. 3. Those who took possession of goods that are Estates of the Empire or belong to them, such as all bishoprics, abbeys and provostries listed in the Imperial matricula. 4. Those who transferred goods to uses other than pious ones. A use is deemed pious, however, if the goods are applied to the poor, to churches and schools admitted in the Empire (Catholic, that is, or of the Augsburg Confession, all others excluded), to the ransoming of captives, and to similar purposes. Thus. Now let us set out here the actual words of the Diet.

units.la: Dieweil aber etliche Stände vnd derselbigen Verfarn/etliche Stifft/Klöster/ vnd andere Geistliche guter eingezogen / vnd dieselbigen zu Kirchen/ Schulen/ milten vnd andern sachen / angewendt. So sollen auch solche eingezogene guter welche den jenigen so dem Reich ohn mittel vnderworffen / vnd Reichs Stände sein nit zugehörig / vnd der Possession die Geistlichen zu zeit deß Passawi- schen vertrags oder sonsten nit gehabt / in diesem Friedenstande / mit begriffen vnd eingezogen seyn / vnd bey der Verordnung wie es ein jeder Stände mit ob- herurten eingezogen / vnd allebereit verwenden guttern / gemacht gelassen werden / vnd diesel bigen Stände dernhalb weder in noch außerhalb Rechtens zu erhaltung eines bestendigen ewigen Friedens nit besprochen noch angefochten werden. Derhalben beuehlen vnd gebieten wir hiemit vnd in krafft dieses Abschiedts der Key. Mai. Cammerichter vnd Beysitzern / das sie diese eingezogener vnd verwendter guter halben kein Citation Mandat vnd Proceß erkennen vnd decernieren sollen. Addere licet Comitia Spirensia a.cIↄlɔxliv. eademque, anni cIↄ lɔ lvii. Iterum Augustana a.cIↄ lɔ lxvi. & Ratilboncusia, a.cIↄ lɔ lxxvi. Hoc ergo ad aeternae pacis observantiam & tum, & nunc necessarium exist imarunt Imperii Ordines, ut bona Ecclesiastica, à quibus illa occupata sint, modo in usus (quod omnino decet) pios applicentur, talia maneant, & quieta perpetuum gaudeant possessione. Pace nupera ita statutum, art. v. §. 3. Bona Ecclesiastica immedi-ata quod attinet, sive sint Archi-Episcopatus, Episcopatus, Praelatura, Abbatia, Balivia, Praepositura, Commenda, sive libera fun-dationes saculares, aut alia una cum reditibus, pensionibus aliisque quocunque nomine signatis, seu in Vrbibus seu rury sitis, ea seu Catholici, seu Augustana Confessionis Status die prima Ianuarii Anni millesimi sexcentesimi vicesimi quarti possederint, omnia & singula nullo plane excepto, ejus religionis Consortes, qui dicto tempore in reali eorum possessione fuerunt, usque dum de Religionis dissidiis per Dei gratiam conventum fuerit, tranquille & imperturbate possideant, neutrique parti liceat alteri seu in Iudicio seu extra, negocium facessere, multo minus turbas aut impedimentum aliquod inferre: Si vero, quod Deus prohibeat, de Religionis dissidiis amicabiliter conveniri non possit, nihilominus hac conventio perpetua sit & pax semper duratura. §. 9. Quecunque Monasteria, Collegia, Balliviae, Commendas, Templa, fundationes scholas, hospitalia, aliaque bona Ecclesiastica mediata, ut & eorum reditus, turaque quoque nomine ea appellata fuerint, Augustanae Confessionis Electores, Principes, Status Anni millesimi sexcentesimi vicesimi quarti, die prima Ianuarii, possedederunt, eadem omnia & singula sive retenta semper, sive restituta, sive vigore hujus Transactionis restituenda, iidem possideant, donec controversia Religionis amicabili partium compositione universalis defi-niantur, non attentis exceptionibus sive post transactionem Passaviensem aut Pacem Religiosam reformata & occupata, aut quod non de vel in territorio Augustana Confessionis Statuum, vel exempta, vel aliis Statibus jure suffraganeatus, Diaconatus, aliave quavis ratione obligata fuisse dicuntur, unicum solumque hujus transactionis, restitutionis, observantiaeque futurae fundamentum sit die prima Ianuarii anno millesimo vicesimo quarto habita possessio, irritis prorsus exceptionibus quae ex introductio alicubi locorum exercitio Interimisticotel autoribus aut jecutis pactis generalibus aut specialibus transactionibus, vel litibus motis causisve decisis, vel etiam decretis, mandatis, rescriptis, paritoriis, reversalibus, litispendentiis vel aliis quibuscunque pretextibus & rationibus deijmi possent. Vbi igitur supradictorum omnium bonorum, eorundem pertinentium, frufructuumve Augustana Confessionis Statibus aliquid quovis modo aut praetextu sive extrajudicialiter à dicto tempore interversum, aut ademptum est, omnino absque mora, & indistincte (interque illa speciali-ter etiam Monasteria, fundationes atque bona Ecclesiastica omnia & singula à Principe VVurtembergico anno millesimo sexcentesimo quarto possessa) cum suis pertinentiis, redditibus & accessionibus ubicunque sitis, una cum omnibus documentum in priorem statum restituantur. Nec Augustanae Confessioni addicti posthac in habita vel recuperata possessione ullo modo turbentur, sed ab omni persecutione juris & facti perpetuo tuti sint, donec controversia Religionis composita fuerint. Unde, quinam pacis perpetui sint inimici, & sibi in Imperii Constitutiones ad pacem servandam omnino necessarias indebitam usurpent potestatem, atque ut illud quod fundamenti loco arripiunt jamdudum sit praejudicatum, apparet. VI. Denique utcunque esset de bonis Ecclesiasticis quod praetendit Papa, non ob eam tamen causam pacem tanti momenti rescindere liceret, vel juxta canones suos, & quod alias quidem ipse egit; nam licitum tali casu se hic est, tantae nimirum pacis causa, bonorum Ecclesiasticorum alienationem negari nequit, dum in canonibus vulgo statuitur, vel ob causam necessitatis, aut pietatis, tum utilitatis Ecclesiae, denique commoditatis, alienare Ecclesiastica bona licere. Stephanus Quaranta, in Summa Bullarii, tit. Alienatio rerum Eccles. Quae fere in hoc nostro casu omnes causae concurrunt. Imo absque consensu Pontificis quaedam ex necessitate alienari posse, docet Molanus, de piis Testam. cap. lxiv. Concessum aliquando, ut bonorum & rerum Ecclesiasticarum pars alienaretur in subsidia belli Turcici: quae ratio erit, ut non idem liceat, (si vel alienatio hic interveniret, quae nec tamen est; sed Ecclesiis, licet non Papalibus, bona sua in usus pios asservantur) ad redimendam tanti operis pacem ac est haec Germaniae? Inter Gravamina imperii tradita in Comitiis Norimbergicis a. MDXXXII. cap. xx dixerunt Principes: Eam ob rem pro licito, bono, ac pariter Christiana reipub. utili & necessario visum placitumque est, ut quando exigere id necessitas vi-debidebitur que mundus & pretiosior supellex ecclesiarum cathedralium, monasteriorum, cateraeque ecclesiarum ac religiosarum domorum, auri, argenti, unionum, aliorumque pretiosorum lapillorum, denique & campanarum pars non necessaria, pro communi Christiana reipub. utilitate in medium conferatur, ne thesaurus ille ecclesiae Turcis potius, quam nobis custodiatur. P. Paulus III. & Iulius II bonorum Ecclesiasticorum in Hispania multam partem Carolo V. donarunt, in bellum contra Protestantes instituendum: dimidiam bonorum partem per Hispaniam; alibi quartam: Historia Concil. Trident. lib. II. & v. Atque netas erit bona Ecclesiastica à Protestantibus occupata, & in usus Ecclesiasticos applicata, & per Imperii foedera illis concessa, quaeque bello repeti nec potuerunt, nec debuerunt, & solenni pacis tractatu jam illis iterum confirmata sunt, Ecclesiis, quam vis non Papalibus, relinquer? Audiamus, quae hanc in re quoque; adfert Iohannes Gerhardi, Theologus doctissimus, in Appendice, ad primum lib. Confess. Catholicae: Ipsimet Pontifici absolute & simpliciter non improbant in certis quibusdam casibus reditus Monasteriorum ad alios usus converti, quam in sustentationem Monachorum; quin & concedunt bona Ecclesiastica certis quibusdam circumstantiis à Principibus Secularibus possideri posse. Actio Perduellionis in Iesuitas (cuius Autor est Pontificius, ut ex multis constat indicis) lit. G. ii. Papst Clemens VIII. hat Hertzog Friedrich von Württemberg durch Andream Cardinal von Oesterreich verschriben lassen, wenn er die Catholische Religion annehme, so wolt er ihm über alle seine Lands Geistliche Güter das Ius Patronatus verleihen, also das einer, zween oder drey seiner Söhne oder Vettern alle diese Klöster in Commendam hetten, den andern, so Weltlich blieben, jährliche Pensiones davon bezahlen, und noch darzu beÿ Straßburg, Cöln, Mainz und andern Fürstlichen Stifften aufgenommen würden. Cajetanus in Comment. 2.2.q.43. art. 8. Ipsa Ecclesia, qua dominium habet bonorum deputatorum ad fabricam, ad stipendia Ministrorum, & ad subsidia pauperum, recte aliquando potest illa donare alius, aut permittere ad vitandum scandalum. Praelati quoque possunt & debent interdum repetitionem illorum differre ad vitandum scandalum & calamitatem pauperum, si Principes ejusmodi bona & jura Ecclesiae sine magno saltem detrimento mento sui Status non possint reddere. Quinimo ipsimet Iesuitæ Ca-sati & Augustiss. Ferdinando autores fuerunt, ut ex Monasteriorum recuperatorum reditibus quosdam ad alios usus converteret; unde sic scribunt Iesuitæ Dillingenses in Placida Disceptat. p. 15. Ex Monasteriis Episcopatibus succurritur, dantur Commendæ bene meritis & accipiuntur. Hoc sacrilegio deputare hominis est leges ignorantis. pag. 24. Cur agre ferrent Ordines Religiosi, quadam Monasteria Cardinalibus & Archiepiscopis cedere? pag. 6. Imperator ratione iustitiæ obligatur, ex Monasteriis recuperatis Ecclesiarum sive Episcopatuum debita dissolvere, dare militibus, Reipubl. opis egentem adjuvare. pag. 34. Episcopi gravia damna passi sunt, as alienum contraxerunt, ipsi auxilio Monasteriorum vacantium egent, petunt & accipiunt. Idem statuit Laymannus Iesuita, in Iusta Defensione in Proem. num. 28.30.31. &c. Atque hæc dicta sunt ad primam & præcipuam causam, quam Papa in Bulla adfert abrogandæ pacis Germanicæ, ex bonis Ecclesiasticis, nempe quod hæc eo pacto in manus Protestantium perveniunt ibique relinquuntur.
units.tr: Since, however, some estates and their predecessors have seized certain foundations, monasteries and other ecclesiastical goods and applied them to churches, schools, charitable purposes and other things, such seized goods shall likewise be included in this peace settlement, namely those held by persons who are subject to the Empire directly and do not belong to the Estates of the Empire, and whose possession the clergy did not have at the time of the Passau treaty or otherwise; and they shall be left as each estate has arranged them with the aforesaid seized and already applied goods; and those estates shall not be called to account or challenged, either within or outside the law, for the sake of maintaining a lasting and eternal peace. We therefore order and command, by this recess, the Imperial Chamber Judge and Assessors that they shall not pass any citation, mandate or process concerning these seized and applied goods, and shall decree none. One may add the Diets of Speyer in 1544, and again in 1557, the Augsburg Diet of 1566, and the Regensburg Diet of 1576. Therefore the Estates of the Empire judged this necessary both then and now for observing the eternal peace: that ecclesiastical goods, from which they were seized, should, provided they are applied to pious uses (as is entirely fitting), remain as they are and enjoy quiet possession forever. In the recent peace it was thus decreed, art. 5, §3: As far as immediate ecclesiastical goods are concerned, whether they be archbishoprics, bishoprics, prelacies, abbeys, bailiwicks, provostries, commendams, or free secular foundations, together with their revenues, pensions and other things under whatever name, whether in towns or in the countryside, which the Catholic or the Augsburg Confession estates possessed on the first day of January in the year 1624, all and each of them, without any exception, shall be held peacefully and undisturbed by the co-religionists who were in actual possession at that time, until the dissensions over religion have been settled by God's grace; and neither party shall be permitted to trouble the other, either in court or outside it, much less to cause disturbance or any hindrance. But if, which God forbid, the dissensions over religion cannot be settled amicably, this agreement shall nonetheless be perpetual and peace shall always endure. §9. Whatever monasteries, colleges, bailiwicks, commendams, churches, foundations, schools, hospitals, and other mediate ecclesiastical goods, together with their revenues, and whatever name they go by, which the Electors, Princes and Estates of the Augsburg Confession possessed on the first day of January 1624, all these, each and every one, whether they have always been retained, or have been restored, or are to be restored by virtue of this agreement, shall be held by the same persons until the controversy over religion is finally settled by a universal amicable agreement of the parties. Exceptions shall not be considered, whether it is said that such goods were reformed and seized after the Passau treaty or the Religious Peace, or that they were situated in, or exempt from, the territory of the Estates of the Augsburg Confession, or were bound to other Estates by the right of suffragan status, diaconate, or some other obligation; the sole and only foundation of this agreement, of the restitution and of future observance shall be the possession held on the first day of January in the year 1624, and all exceptions shall be utterly void which could be brought forward on account of the introduction of the Interim somewhere, or from the exercise of it, or from general or special agreements or transactions made in consequence, or from lawsuits brought or cases decided, or even from decrees, mandates, rescripts, writs of execution, reversals, pending litigation, or any other pretexts and grounds whatsoever. Therefore, where any of the aforesaid goods, and their dependencies, fruits or income, have in any way or under any pretext, whether extrajudicially, been taken away or removed from the Estates of the Augsburg Confession since the said time, they shall all be restored to their former state, at once and without distinction (among which, especially, the monasteries, foundations and all ecclesiastical goods, each and every one, possessed by the Württemberg Prince in the year 1604), together with their appurtenances, revenues and accessions, wherever they are situated, along with all documents. Nor shall adherents of the Augsburg Confession henceforth be disturbed in any way in the possession they hold or have recovered, but shall be safe from every persecution, legal or actual, forever, until the controversy over religion has been settled. Hence it appears who are the enemies of perpetual peace, and who arrogate to themselves an undue power over the constitutions of the Empire that are wholly necessary for keeping the peace, and that what they take up as a foundation has long since been prejudged. VI. Finally, whatever the Pope may claim about ecclesiastical goods, it would not on that account be permitted to annul so weighty a peace, nor, according to his own canons (which in other matters he himself has followed), could the alienation of ecclesiastical goods be refused in such a case, since in the canons it is commonly laid down that ecclesiastical goods may be alienated for the sake of necessity, or of piety, or of the utility of the Church, and finally of convenience. Stephanus Quaranta, in the Summa Bullarii, under the title Alienatio rerum Eccles., lists these reasons, nearly all of which concur in our present case. Indeed, Molanus teaches, in de piis Testam. ch. 64, that without the Pope's consent some goods may be alienated out of necessity. It was once granted that part of the ecclesiastical goods and property might be alienated for the subsidies of the Turkish war. If that is so, why should it not likewise be permitted, to purchase the peace of Germany, so great a matter, to alienate (if indeed any alienation takes place here, which it does not; rather, the Churches, though not Papal ones, keep their goods for pious uses)? In the Grievances of the Empire presented at the Nuremberg Diet of 1532, ch. 20, the Princes said: For that reason it has been judged and resolved to be lawful, good, and equally useful and necessary for the Christian commonwealth, that when necessity seems to demand it, a part of the unnecessary movables and more precious furnishings of cathedral churches, monasteries and other churches and religious houses, of gold, silver, pearls, other precious stones, and finally of the bells, shall be contributed for the common utility of the Christian commonwealth, lest that treasure of the Church be kept for the Turks rather than for us. Popes Paul III and Julius II gave a large part of the ecclesiastical goods in Spain to Charles V, to be used for waging war against the Protestants: half the goods throughout Spain, and elsewhere a quarter. History of the Council of Trent, books II and V. And shall ecclesiastical goods that have been seized by the Protestants and applied to ecclesiastical uses, and that were granted to them by the covenants of the Empire, which could neither be, nor ought to be, reclaimed by war, and which have been confirmed to them again by a solemn peace treaty, be left to the Churches, though not Papal ones? Let us hear what Johann Gerhard, a most learned theologian, adduces on this point in the Appendix to the first book of the Confessio Catholica: The Pope himself does not absolutely and simply disapprove of the revenues of monasteries being turned to other uses than the support of monks in certain cases; indeed, they even concede that ecclesiastical goods may in certain circumstances be possessed by secular princes. The Actio Perduellionis against the Jesuits (whose author is a Papist, as is clear from many indications), page G ii, relates: Pope Clement VIII had Duke Friedrich of Württemberg assured through Cardinal Andreas of Austria that, if he accepted the Catholic religion, he would grant him the right of patronage over all his ecclesiastical goods in his lands, so that one, two or three of his sons or cousins could hold all these monasteries in commendam, while the others who remained secular would be paid annual pensions from them, and besides, he would be admitted to the princely foundations at Strasbourg, Cologne, Mainz and other princely chapters. Cajetan, in his Commentary on 2.2, q. 43, art. 8: The Church itself, which has ownership of goods assigned for building, for the stipends of ministers and for the support of the poor, may sometimes rightly give them to another, or permit it, to avoid scandal. Prelates too may and sometimes should defer their reclaiming of such goods, to avoid scandal and the calamity of the poor, if the Princes cannot restore such goods and rights of the Church without at least great detriment to their own state. Indeed the Jesuits themselves, Casati and the most august Ferdinand, were the authors of his converting some of the revenues of the recovered monasteries to other uses; whence the Jesuits of Dillingen write thus in the Placida Disceptatio, p. 15: From the monasteries assistance is given to bishoprics; commendams are given to the well deserving and received by them. To count this as sacrilege is the mark of a man ignorant of the laws. p. 24: Why should religious orders be annoyed that some monasteries yield to cardinals and archbishops? p. 6: The Emperor is bound by the reason of justice to pay off, from the revenues of recovered monasteries, the debts of churches or bishoprics, to give to soldiers, and to help the Commonwealth when it is in need of aid. p. 34: Bishops have suffered grave losses and have contracted debts; they themselves need, seek and accept the help of vacant monasteries. Laymann, a Jesuit, lays down the same in his Iusta Defensio, in the Proem, nos. 28, 30, 31, etc. These things have been said against the first and principal reason which the Pope adduces in the Bull for abrogating the German peace, namely, that the ecclesiastical goods, by this agreement, pass into the hands of the Protestants and are left there.

units.la: In quibus ideo diligentiores nos esse oportuit, quia ad bene diluendam Papæ & Papanorum adversus Nos objectionem, super bonis Ecclesiasticis, illud amoliendum ab Ecclesiis & doctrina nostra convitium fuit, cui ceu primæ rationi adeoque principali superstruitur Papalis abrogatio & condemnatio Germanicæ pacis, quasi vellemus bona Ecclesiastica (Ecclesiastica intrepide, uti nunc abunde vidimus, primi, omnesque Reformationis Doctores loquuntur) id est, Ecclesiæ Christi, in usus Ecclesiasticos data legataque, contra naturam suam, haud in Ecclesiæ, sed privatorum usus, impendi. Quibus nihil derogant quę nuper Vir doctus, quemq; magni alias facio, commentatus est, de Canonicis &c. Quo in scripto diffusam quidem suam prodidit (fateor) lectionem, sed hanc fere unam, judicium parce, æquitatem & reverentiam cum erga alios, tum erga Præceptorem suum venerandum, pessime: ex quo pravo unice affectu cum procusus liber ille sit, quod ego sane doleo, dolebit, & ipse (sat scio) Auctor, ubi provectior evaserit, vel is,quem tam indigne nunc insectatur, olim mortuus desiderabitur, momentum suum apud Lectores bonæ ac compositæ mentis suo merito perdidit. Quid obsecro est, rem non posse a gi absque contumeliis? non inter eruditos? neque rem tantam, quæ (li quæ alia) defæcatum poscit judicium, & compositam bene mentem? Siccine vincitur, quando dilaniatis aliorum, quos semper vel ætatis, ordinis, aut officiorum erga te ratione suspicere tenearis, nominibus, illis procaciter infultas; & neque quod aliis Deus copiose admensus est, agnoscere vis, neque eo quod tibi datum, bene uti? sed justo inde Dei fit judicio, ut agitatus ejusmodi consiliis, dum nec agis, quod debes, hoc neque etiam agas, quod agere videaris. Certe id in libro (quem dico) observare in proclivi est, qui ubi à proprio Auctore quandoque sedata magis mente fuerit releɛtus, extra illos, in quibus conceptus enixusque est animi fluctus, opinor, quod si non rem, saltem agendi tractandique modum, improbaturus ipse tandem fit. Ad exemplum scilicet, cujus hic recordor, Andreæ Zebedæi (de quo volo ut legas integrum illum paragraphum, quem Beza in vita Calvini facit ad a. 1555. judicelque ut ista huc applicari bene possint) qui postquam diu acriterque & variis calumniis Calvino adversatus fuisset, Calvino mortuo; cum & ipse jam esset moriturus, Neviduni, oppido quatuor milliaribus Geneva distante, accitis præcipuis civibus, ultro agnita, quā oppugnârat, veritate, & acta illa sua detestans, schedas omnes suas spectante se concremari jussit. Quippe re ipsa Noster hic nec uti debuit, neq; uti velint, quibus patrocinatus videtur, cepit. Quatuor ejus in tota disputatione sut hypotheses quibus innititur, quibusque, luxatis vel ablatis omnis illa (ipsum non respuo hic judicem) corruit: in quibus omnibus quam graviter aberrarit, digito duntaxat ostendam, quia ego non materiam nunc hanc ingredi cogito, sed quod mea disputatio requirit solummodo ostendam ac tuebor, sententiam Ecclesiæ esse non aliam ac antea ex Doctoribus nostris asseasserui, quod nempe bona Ecclesiastica in Ecclesiasticos, non in privatorum usus impendenda sunt. Primo disputat, quasi in re illa quam versat, agatur solum de bonis Ecclesiarum idololatricis, id est, Ecclesiæ, led in solos usus idololatricos & superstitiosos concessis, quasi vel alia nulla bona Ecclesia habeat, puta videlicet à superstitione, vel de iis quoque non controvertatur. Saltem ergo sinat quæcunque bona deprehenduntur Ecclesiis, pauperibusque data, extra usum idololatricum & superstitiosum, illis ipsis, quibus data, salva constare & integra, extraque suam, quam facit disputationem ea haberi,& conclusionem. Perpetuo autem ipsum disputationem figere in bonis idololatricis, apparet ex pag. 28. 97. 228.229.231.239.289.325.&c. unde etiam passim bona idolo- latrica, & pseudo Ecclesiastica appellat. Quamvis quidem multa sub Papatu, & ejus κτημ maxime à seculo nono, uti dicis pag. 28. donata Ecclesiis sint ex opinione meriti, & pro redimendis animis &c. neutiquam tamen dicendum, vel omnes erroneis his opinionibus imbutos, vel omnes donationes fallo huic fundamento superstructas fuisse. Et ut hoc sit, non idem spero pronunciabis de tempore, quo declinare Papismus cepit, & in occasum suum vergere; denique non de seculis anterioribus, de medio tempore, uti dicis pag. 13. quo, post Constantinum, magna etiam erga Ecclesiam fuit Principum privatorumque liberalitas, quando multi integras facultates Ecclesiis consecrabant, uti ex Basilio ostendis; vel qu oufque Germanos ad Christum conversos, à doctrinâ Antichristi integros facis pag. 83.ad tepora fc. Bonifacii Moguntini archiepiscopi, quod fuit a. Dcccxlv. Successit autem Willibrordo in Episcopatu Vltrajectino; quo tempore Ecclesias Germanicas egregie à Francorum Regibus aliisque dotatas fuisse, præterquam ex diplomatibus,& præcedentium donationum confirmationibus, sub Bonifacio illo, à Pipino Rege factis, patet insuper ex contentione hoc tempore orta inter Ecclesiam Trajectensem nostram,& Coloniensem, archiepiscopo Coloniense afferente, ad se pertinere Trajectensem, ex donatione Regis Dagoberri; contra Trajectense, se immediate spectare ad sedem Romanam: verum nostra adversus Colonienlem magnis opibus abundantem, inquit Beka, stare non potuit. Quae itaque hic usque data Ecclesiis fuere, pro antichristianis censeri neutiquam debent. Verum ipsa Diplomata inspiciantur, ad haec enim redit disputatio, eaque audienda hic quam primum esse res ipsa loquitur, & quis renuat? Liquebit sane varia fuisse legata Ecclesiis, omissa omni Papalis superstitionis opinione mentioneque, vel alias tenuiter satis ea significata. Reperies, ex amore Dei. ad Honorem Dei. divini cultus amore. in sustentationem Clericorum, ut orationibus vacarent jugiter, pro impetranda in judicio extremo misericordia. ad casam Dei. ad peragendum Dei servitium. ad opus Ecclesiae. Donamus Deo. In honore Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Ob Dei amorem. Dei timoris causa. Propter Deum. usitata fere formula. Cum petitionibus sacerdotum justis & rationabilibus divini cultus amore favemus, remunerationem hujus rei a Christi gratia expectamus, ut in diplomate Regis Conradi, sub Rabbodo episcopo legitur. Ad reformandum, & confirmandum religionis cultum, in Diplomate Dagoberti, Francorum Regis, a. dcxxxix. Alibi, ut in servitio Dei semper vacarent. Propter nomen Domini, vel amorem caelestem. Pro Dei amore. In Diplomate Hincmari, aliorumque Episcoporum, in Synodo Vermerianensi, a. d. cccclxx. In usus, dicunt, luminariorum, matricularium, & caeteris, quae in Ecclesiis, in praefato Monasterio Vedalti positis necessaria fuerint. Ibidem: ad Hospitale verorum pauperum &c. & haec, & illa. In Diplomate, eidem Monasterio concessio a Carolo Calvo: in futuro providentes, si quo modo possimus saluti fidelium & Ecclesiarum Christi providere stabilitati. In alio: Ut non deficiat in eis (vid. Ecclesiis) Laus Dei de ore hominum, & Christianae religionis sacer cultus, unde mortales ad beatitudinem adspirant. Balduinus Hierosolymitanus a. clo lxxxi. in Diplomate, pro aedificando in urbe Valentiniana templo: Qui locus ne divinis vacaret cultibus, clericos ibidem ad Deo serviendum constituimus. Alias: ibidem Domino servientium usibus profutura in aeternum. Ad augmentum servitii Dei, Dei. Pro divini cultus augumento. Pro conversione infidelium, quos exponere, uti facit Nolter pag.83. de Christianis, sed non copositis ad regulam factionis Antichristianæ, misera & ridicula profecto crisis est. Sed Bonifacii legatio instituta legitur apud Aventinum, ad Gentium illuminationem, quum tamen jam in Germania essent Christianæ Ecclesiæ. Resp. Fuerunt ante Bonifacium, ante Willibrordum quoque in Germania Ecclesiæ Christi nomen professæ, neque per illos demum Christianismus in has regiones introductus, post verbum Evangelicum jam dudum in inferiore Germania seminatum, inquit Heda, in exordio suæ Historiæ, advenere huc ex Anglia Willebrordus, aliique; sed nemo nisi Historiarum ignorantissimus negaverit etiam plurima adhuc loca temporibus Bonifacii, ac Willibrordi Gentilismo addicta fuisse, pro quibus ad Christianam religionem adducendis illi sc. laborarunt, & missi præcipue sunt, utcunque etiam pro seculi errore plus æquo Papæ Romano servire instituerint. Atque illos intelligendos esse per Gentiles, quibus illuminandis destinati fuerint; idololatras, paganos, infideles, non Christianos ad disciplinam Romanensem perducendos, certissimum. Vbi enim unquam tu legeris, Christianos doctrinam Christi professos, infideles dici, vel Gentiles, vel paganos, atque ab ipsis Christianis, & Christianismi Doctoribus? sane Egbertus Anglus, qui Willibrordum in has oras misit; uti ante eum, Wigbertum, dicitur tum hinc, tum istum misisse, ut ibidem infideli populo veritatem prædicaret Evangelicam. Willibrordus etiam, discipulos in terminos suæ diæcesis, ad Evangelizandum infideli populo doctrinam æternæ beatitudinis destinasse; & Bonifacius, apud Moguntiam, verbum æternæ beatitudinis prædicare cepisse, & Francos cum Thuringis ab infidelitatis errore convertisse, & ad infidelem Frisiæ populum accessisse, à quo etiam trucidatus fuit. Illosne Christianos dixeris? vel quando Gentiles audis, & Willibrordi discipulum Adelbertum, post plurimorum Gentilium conversionem, & sic Suidbertum, in Domino obiisse, cogitabis, Christianos ad alterius sc.Romanæ Ecclesiæ disciplinam adductos?etiam, ubi legis de Willebrordo, vel Clemente, nam sic à Papa Sergio appellatus fuit: accidit itidem sanctum Clementem visitare. gentilem populum sua diaecesis in Walachria, ubi simulachrum Mercurii colebatur in magna reverentiâ, cujus statuam idem sanctus Antistes extemplo confregit, & prophanum idolum dedignanter abjecit? vel, quod Bonifacius ipse convertisse populum dicitur à barbarâ gentilitatis idololatriâ? & in Germaniam venisse, ut prophanum idolalatriæ cultum aboleret, ac rudem populum documentis Evangelicis informaret? quod in conversione paganorum praedicator fuerit inclytus, expques tu scilicet de Christianis? In epistola, quam Bonifacius scripsit ad Stephanum Papam, narrat, quomodo Willebrordus à Papa Sergio fuerit missus, ad praedicandam paganam gentem Frisonum in littoribus Oceani Occidui, quam magna ex parte converterit ad fidem Christianam, fana & delubra destruxerit &c. sed quod jam Colonien-sis episcopus controversiam ei moveat, asserens Trajectinam Ecclesiam ad se pertinere, ex hoc quidem fundamento, quod ecclesia in castello Trajecto olim erecta, postea autem à Paganis diruta, sibi à Francorum Rege Dagoberto, una cum Castello; attributa fuisset, quam Willebrordus postea iterum exstruxit, & S. Martino consecravit. Vbi urgebat Bonifacius, ea conditione donata esse Coloniensi illa, ut gentem Frisonum ad fidem converteret, & eorum praedicator esset: quod quia ipse non praedicavit, non convertit Frisones ad fidem Christi, sed pagana mansit gens Fresonum, usque ad praedicationem Willibrordi, indecens existimabat Bonifacius, ut alteri, quam Romano Pontifici, subjecta esset Trajectina Ecdes, praedicans genti Fresonum, quia magna pars gentis illius adhuc pagana erat. Quis hominum illa unquam aliter quam de gentilibus nondum Christo initiatis intelligat? qui, quamvis hic ibi nonnulli Christiani & ecclesiæ Christianæ erant, maximam tamen turbam faciebant, & à quibus indesinenter graviterque vexabantur Christiani, opprimebanturque, etiam nostro hoc in loco; jam à Frisiis, tum Saxonibus, Danis, & Normannis. Easque causa erat Bonifacio, Moguntia relicta, post mortem Willibrordi huc commeandi, videlicet ne populus per prædicationem suam dudum conversus ad idololatriam seftam redivet, uti Iohannes de Beka scribit, in suo Chronico. Vnde jam, quando in antiquarum donationum diplomatibus mentio fit aut Gentilium, aut conversionis eorundem, sole clarius est, non alios intelligendos esse quam ethnicos idololatras, qui illis temporibus adhuc multi erant convertendi ad fidem Christianam, nullo autem modo veros Christianos, & qui ad regulam factionis Antichristianæ, ad quam nondum erant compositi, essent adducendi, uti temere vult Auctor libri quem præ manibus habemus, pag.83. qui idem tamen quando pag. 386 ait, Carolum Magnum Ecclesias fundasse, præpositis iis Clericis, non solum ut per hos quasi Paganismus propelleretur, Christianaque religio propagaretur &c. inquit, in quibus annon sibi adversetur, & hic intelligat conversionem paganorum, Ethnicorum ad Christianam religionem; ita ut non illo seculo per Gentiles intellecti fuerint non compositi ad regulam Antichristianam, ipse viderit. Ipsa nunc audiamus, istorum temporum, aliqua diplomata quibus pro conversione gentilium, donationes Ecclesiis factæ sunt. Post Bonifacium, sub Gregorio, tertio Ecclesiæ Trajectinæ Episcopo, Carolus Rex in confirmatione donationum, ab Antecessoribus suis factarum, sic loquitur: ad ipsam causam Dei, per eorum testamenta, ut in luminariis seu stipendiis Monachorum, atque Canonicorum, qui ibidem Gentiles ad Christianitatem convertunt, & Domini misericordia ipsos conversos, quos habent, doceant, juxta quod Christiani eorum Christianitatem conservant. Qui alii Gentiles, nisi Christianis oppositi, atque ad Christianitatem convertendi? quique ibidem adhuc erant, post primos episcopos. Æquis Christianos, & illos quidem optimos dixerit Gentiles, ¬arit ita palam, & in donationibus? nemo vel Paparum Romanorum producetur ita loquutus unquam fuisse, nemo Imperatorum, vel aliorum, de Christianis, de illis quos utcunque ad normam factionis Romanæ compositos vellent: neque tantum isto adhuc tempore discrimen inter Christianismum & Papismum; neque illis locis quispiam prudens aut sanæ mentis illud si vel fuisset, tali pacto designasset, Christianos, non Romanenses, ideo Gentiles nominando, vel infideles, vel paganos. Denique si forte etiam Gentilium censu habiti fuissent tales, non simpliciter tamen Gentiles fuissent appellati, nisi addita qua pleniori explicatione & distinctione à communiter notis, & isto tempore, locoq; adhuc obviis gentilibus, præsertim in testamentis, & donationibus, ubi semper, & ab illis hoc quoque tum observatum, apertissime & pluribus verbis modisque res, extra omne dubium, quo fit, exponi solet In diplomate Ludovici Imperatoris, sub Rixfrido episcopo: ita & procuratores Reip. de eadem decima parte accipere aut usurpare ad fiscum non præsumant, qualiter Præsul ipsius Ecclesiæ, cum omni Clero & populo sibi subjecto alimoniam ministrare, & Luminaria in eadem sede continuare, atque Gentiles qui ad Christianitatem convertuntur alere & docere possit. Et in fine: Sicut à Domino Imperatore, & avo nostro, & antecessoribus Regibus à nobis per hanc authoritatem constitutum est, atque confirmatum, ita omni tempore inviolabiliter conservetur atque custodiatur, quatenus ipsos Jervos Dei, qui ibidem constiterunt cum eorum Pontifice, & illos quos à gentili ritu ad Christi veram converterunt fidem, pro nobis, conjuge, proleque nostra, & omni populo Christiano jugiter misericordiam Dei exorare delectet. A Gentili ritu ad Christi veram conversi fidem, diceturne de Christianis ad regulam Romanæ Ecclesiæ adducti? vel quid illud ante hnjusmodi conversionem tam discordans à similitudine Romanæ Ecclesiæ, ut proinde dici debuerint Gentiles, vel opus ut habuerint tanta cóversione, illumq; in finem constitutæ sint tam amplæ Ecclesiis donationes? aut quæ illa forma Ecclesiæ Romanæ adeo commendata, nondum enim Papismus eo tempore ad ἀκμὴν pervenerat, ut ad illam perducti tum demum habendi fuissent pro Christianis, & conversis? sed vereor ne plus, quam dignum sit, operæ insumere judicer, in explodenda temeraria ista crisi, qua Auctor censuit per Gentiles, eorumrumque conversionem, quando in istorum temporum Actis memorantur, non intelligendos Gentiles, ethnicos, idololatras, sed veros Christianos, ast ad regulam factionis Antichristianæ componendos. Hoc forte unus statuat, nisi jam aliter sit edoctus, certè, alios in eandem sententiam secum ituros haud multum metuo. Quid autem id est? Gregorius ad Bonifacium scribens, ei gratulatur, quod Deus inter illas gentes viam salutis, & ostium misericordiæ aperuerit: ergo per gentes, intelliguntur Christiani. cur non gentes paganæ? quomodo ad Papam Stephanum scribit ipse Bonifacius. Vel quid illud est argumentari: In Synodo Metensi a. 864 Normanni & Dani vocantur pagani, quum quadraginta ante annos illis prædicarit quidam Haraldus; ergo non intellexit Synodus Normanos paganos, sed Christianos: vel, ergo non erat amplius ulli Normanni pagani? vel non saltem illi, quos arceri Synodus velit. In Diplomate Otthonis I. a. lo ccccxlviii. dato Gemblacensi Monasterio adhuc legitur: à falsis quatenus Christianis, vel paganis &c. adeo ut isto necdum tempore immunes à Paganorum impetu atq; oppressione fuerint Christiani. Pagani Christianis opponuntur, alibi idcirco infideles appellati. In Diplomate Regis Dagoberti. a. Ioxl. Et si propter Paganorum, vel infidelium, vel Christianorum devastationem. verum hæc mitto. Satis vidimus, quomodo, præterquam in alios sacros usus, finesque à Papali superstitione remotos; uti Noster loquitur, non compositos ad regulam factionis Antichristianæ; vel uti ibidem, integros eosque à doctrina Antichristi, plurima Ecclesiis data fuerint bona, ita quoque in conversionem gentilium, & conversorum sustentationem legata quam plurima fuisse. Sequitur ergo, quod ante omnia in hoc negotio agendum esse semper dico, inde inchoandum, & à qua conscientiarum instructione hæc super re ac tranquillatio petenda, ut inspiciantur ipsę donationum & bonorum Ecclesiasticorum fundationes ac diplomata, ex quibus tum de usu bonorum solide judicare possis. Hoc certe nihil æquius; tum ut ex iis constet, quæ bona pura, in sacros usus data sint, quæ vero aliqua forte superstitionis nota commaculata, in quibus tu fundas perpetuam disputationis& exceptionum tuarum basim:tum quia jus & ratio dictant, ut quomodo & secundum quae de aliis bonis, cadem, certe non iniquiori ratione, de ecclesiasticis pronunciemus, & quo pacto nos velimus servatas nostras in donationibus vel legationibus supremas voluntates ac dispositiones, pari quoque reverentia ut versemur erga Majorum nostrorum, praecipue pia, instituta. Nolumus nos frustrari nostras ultimas voluntates,praesertim in rebus religiosis, quare expresse testamento id cavemus ne fiat: uti Philippus Mornayus in suo Testamento, pag. 12. fans en pouvoir estre divertie:neque erga Majorum Testamenta,idem tantis diris postulantia, eandem nos, simili in causa, adhibebimus, religionem? Nulla autem ratione donationibus stare sustinent qui forte nobis hic adversantur, ut ex illarum praescripto lis omnis decidatur, quod tamen aequissimum & certissimum foret: ex adverso supprimere illas velle aut obscurare, ipsum non ingenuae disputationis est & grave praejudicium. Praesertim cum etiam ad intentionem donationum passim se hic referant summi quique e Nostris Doctores, Lutherus, Melanchton, Calvinus, Bucerus, & passim quivis, etiam in locis, a viro docto (sed quae ex MS. Theologorum, quos tantopere insectatur describit,) adductis. Pag. apud ipsum 281. Calvinus consilium Buceri,de bonis illis disponendis dilaudans:quoniam ea lege legata sunt bona, quae hodie tenent Canonici &c. inquit. pag. 200. Melanthon: & propter hanc causam a piis Regibus & Principibus hae opes Ecclesiis, quas nunc tenent, donata sunt cb quae immerito mox Nostro vapulat, quod nimis exegetice & praeter rationem exaggerat define quarumcumque donationum. Atque id ipsum Ordines Generales jusserunt publico edicto a. cIↄ Iↄcxxx. ut in negotio bonorum Ecclesiasticorum agri Silvaeducensis diligenter diplomata fundationum inspicerentur; ex quibus liqueret, an juris Laicalis essent, ut multi dicebant; an vero ad Quaestorem bonorum Ecclesiasticorum deferenda. Quare ut etiam sit juxta Auctoris nostri mentem, qui tototam suam disputationem format de bonis pseudo Ecclesiasticis & idololatricis, ut haec ad usus privatorum applicentur; saltem ergo eximenda ex hoc censu erunt bona vere & pure Ecclesiastica, data in usum Ecclesiae, vel pauperum, adde Scholarum, nulla mentione interiecta erroris, aut superstitionis Papalis. Atque haec censeo, ex omnium confessione, debere cedere illis usibus, quibus pie legata fuere. Quippe ut bene dixit Saravia,lib.de Sacrileg. cap. iv. ut admissam olim donationes multas factas esse, partim superstitiosas, partim nimias, inde non efficitur, nullas fuisse legitimas, pias, Deo gratas, & cum Dei verbo consentaneas, & Ecclesiae utiles ac necessarias. Cetera quod spectat, per Papisimi pravam doctrinam opinionesque defoedata, inspiciatur quantus error commissus sit; & annon oporteat, ex sensu Reformationis, hunc emendare, & servare tamen illa ad usus pios, atque analogos: quemadmodum judicatum supra a variis Reformationis Doctoribus audivimus. Vel exquirantur, quaestione & casu ex formula seu diplomate donationum formato, quorumcumque Theologorum,& Iurisconsultorum Reformatorum sententiae, ut ex iis hac in re agatur, quod ex aequo videbitur. Fateor quippe lubens, de bonis Ecclesiastico Papalibus, ut non idem ubique; casus, ita nec eandem apud omnes deprehendi sententiam: sed, ut Papisimi errores alii aliis graviores sunt, & plus vel minus ab hominibus semper accepti, expressique, sic Reformati hic judicent, quid ex sententia Reformatorum, de illis bonis statuendum sit,& quomodo ubique servanda, quoufq; fieri poterit, & corrigenda, promovendaque sint pia quorumcumque vota, & facta. Facile absque tumultu, litigio, praejudicio cujuscumq;, sententia Doctorum interrogari hic possunt; & sic demum tranquillari conscientia alicujus de bonis quae possidet, poterit, ubi qualis illa natura habeantur, certo & vere constiterit. Adeo in argumentatione, vel syllogismo Auctoris, perpetuo negamus nos utramque propositionem; tum, quod bona aliqua Ecclesiastica Papalis superstitionis fermento inquinata ideo liceat in privatos, non Ecclesiasticos, usus impendere: tum, quod bona omnia, de quibus quaeritur, talia sint. Secundam hanc sternit Auctor hypothesim, ex qua procedit, quasi tantū de superfluo bonorum qualiumcunque Ecclesiasticorum quaestio sit, & de eo solo agatur: quum controversia sit non de superfluo, sed de natura, usuque bonorum Ecclesiasticorum, in se. Quod si autem velit, bonis Ecclesiasticis in usus, quibus data, impensis, ne opum Ecclesiasticarum abundantia tum Ecclesiae, tum Reipub. obsit, superfluum etiam ad alia, quam Ecclesiastica, collocari posse, dum prius illud maneat de Ecclesiasticis bonis natura sua in Ecclesiastica impendendis, iterum concedimus, ut auditis Doctorum super eo sententiis, statuatur quid è re & bono tum Ecclesiae, tum politiae videatur. Sed ut primo tamquam consensissimi juris, puré Ecclesiastica, non alibi, quam hic impendantur; & de superfluo nulla ātē institutur deliberatio, nisi postquam Ecclesiae bene ubiq; provisum sit. Quippe scio variantes hic Doctorum esse sententias. Idem Calvinus, de consensu Theologorum hac in re, scripsit ad Farellum, epistolā illa, quam antea adduximus, scripta a.cl5 l5 xlv. d. xiii. Octob. & certe vix unquam hoc vitium, quo cum vobis certamen nunc est, loquitur de usu bonorum Ecclesiasticorum, corrigetur, nisi Ecclesiarum consensu. Se interim quod attinet, ait in concionibus, in senatu identidem increpuisse temerarios bonorum illorum occupatores. tantum cogitare operae pretium est, inquit in fine, quousque contendere expedit. Vicissim ubi consensus habetur, quemadmodum in bonis vere Ecclesiasticis, eorumque usu Ecclesiastico, magnae temeritatis est, ci tum se velle opponere. Vti in Vicariatibus, ad solos Ecclesiae Ministros impendendis, conveniunt omnes, quos Auctor noster tam indigne exagitat, Ministri (non intendo, quod ille admordet, Mf. dubito mihi an unquam visum); sed omnium consensus in eo est consignatus, improbandam, praeter beneficiorum Ecclesiasticorum emtionem aut venditionem, esse Vicariatum ad alia, quam ad S. Ministerium erogationem: quae ipsa tamen etiam Noster susq; deque habet. Qux Quæ autem ratio in Vicariatibus est, eadem in aliis ubique attendenda, videlicet illi quum donati fundatique sint ad divinum ministerium, recte docetur, in omni horum bonorum negotio respiciendas fundationes, atque ex iis de illorum usu pronunciandum esse. Quod illud unicum est, quod in tota hac disputatione, (ingenuæ probæque profecto causæ vel id solum argumentum, Θ γάρ εστιν ἀνθρώπων ἀφελείας) urgemus ut fiat. Primum est, ut quæ Ecclesiis debentur (semper cum Ecclesiis etiam pauperes complector, aliasque pias causas) utpote Ecclesiis data, legataque, illi tribuantur: neque enim aliter superfluum intelligi, vel haberi potest, quod non est nisi quod superabundat, vel restat ex bonis Ecclesiasticis, postquam nempe ad usus Ecclesiasticos applicata fuerint: & hoc ergo primo loco habeatur: deinde de superfluo confissum. Quod non nisi consentiente tum Ecclesia fieri potest. Auctor noster, pag. 239. Namque Magistratus agnoscit bona Ecclesiastica, & vult esse talia; eo non nisi consentiente, aut saltem in partes veniente (ut Sectione secunda circa bona Parochialia susius ostendemus) Ecclesia alienare potest. Sed ubi; & quando superfluum æstimabitur? vel ex cujus hoc pendebit judicio? quæ nisi primo decidantur, frustra superfluum urges. Ais, te ad exemplum Tigurinorum, qui bona sua Ecclesiastica distribuerunt in usum ministrorum Ecclesiæ, tum Scholarum, te idem semper ut fiat exoptare, primamque curam geri Ministrorum & Scholarum, pag. 191. Si Magistratus aliunde iis; quam ex bonis ecclesiasticis prospicere non queat: & si queat aliunde, annon tamen primam curam geri à Magistratu velis Ministrorum Scholarumque? vel, non ex bonis ecclesiasticis? aut quare primum ex bonis ecclesiasticis, si aliunde illis prospici neque at? nisi quod ecclesiastica primum in usus ecclesiasticos eroganda satis vides: idque antequam de superfluo disputetur: bene, quomodo idem pag. 353 quoque vicariatus reditus non posse ministro ægeno denegari à Patrono scribit; si ex bonis Parochialibus commode familiam sustentare non queat Minister, ipsique destituto Vicariatus reditibus, tuendum fit cum fame; excusari neutiquam potest Patronus, si immerenti subducat tales vica-riatus reditus, etiamsi ipse illos non percipiat, constetque, eos aut pau-peribus, aut Theologiæ studiosis cedere. quæ ratio, nisi quia Vicariatus in alimoniam ministrorum fundati & constituti sunt? Nolumus, inquit pag.198. aut nobilibus, aut aliis quibuscumque, ex massa bonorum quasi Ecclesiasticorum, Magistratus aut horitate ante aliquid cedi, quam prospectum fuerit Ecclesiis, Scholis, & quantum lex prudentia dictat, etiam pauperibus. De superfluo (solum videri vult disputare) postquam Ecclesiis reliquisque cum suis censeri solitis, prospectum, pag.220. & 324. Magistratus prius ex massa bonorum Ecclesiasticorum curam Ecclesiæ, Scholarum, & pauperum, quod ad ordinarios & extraordinarios casus gerit, pag. seq. abunde prospexit. Pag. 562. Quum vero tum prima, tum secunda sectione sapius a nobis prasuppositum fuerit, non posse Magistratum Christianum atque Orthodoxum de superfluo quasi bonorum Ecclesiasticorum in ullius privati commodum disponere, nisi postquam sufficienter prospexerit Ecclesiis, Scholis, atque ratione casuum extraordinariorum pauperibus quoque. adde pag.151.155. 212.216.309.388.&c. quibus identidem inculcat, se non disputare nisi de bonorum Ecclesiasticorum superfluo, postquam abunde Ecclesiis, pauperibus, Scholisque prospectum: & non finit quempiam aliquid ex bonis istis accipere, antequam viderit, abunde provisum Ecclesiis, scholis, pauperibus. Prius ergo Ecclesiæ, Scholæ, pauperesque audiri debent, num forte egeant, & quamdiu hic ostendi possunt necessitates atque indigentiæ, nemini fas bona illorum attingere. Hoc observetur, & sic certe, antequam de superfluo fructra disputamus, arbitror tam bene ecclesiastica bona omnia in usus Ecclesiarum, pauperum, & Scholarum, neque eos superfluos, distribuenda fore, ut cautum conscientiis hominum melius futurum sit, ne se præcipitata bonorum illorum occupatione adeo facile pregravent. Videlicet ubi consideraverimus, tum quis defectus & inopia plerumque Ministrorum sit, quanta egestas vulgo ruralium Ministrorum, viduarum, orphanorum, quæ templorum & Ecclesiarum de novo multis in locis eri-gen. gendarum necessitas; similitèt Scholarum, & quæ huc pertinent;tum quanta pauperum,inopũ,debiliũ vulgo calamitas; quæ exulibus, peregrinis exhibenda sint ; quæ institui egregia possent pro curanda infidelium conversione, & conversorum, vel quæ requirantur ad eorum, qui ex'Papatu', atque aliunde ad Ecclesiam accedunt, sustentatione, quæ nunc ex defectu opum & mediorum multum negliguntur; quæ Ecclesiis exteris, aliisque, oppressis, dispersis, vastatis auxilia suppeditanda; quę sive ad studiorum, sive religionis prosectus & promotionem agitari è re esset, & similia pia opera, ad quæ donata Ecclesiis bona illa sunt,neq; ut præsentibus solũ,sed & absentibus,& futuris,per ea consulamus. His omnibus provisum ubique, vel apud nos etiam satis esse nemo sciens dixerit, qui vel solum inopiam eleemosynarię consideret, commodissimè curandæ; si ei ex bonorum Sacrorũ,massa adjudicétur,quæ isti fini data à Majoribus pie fuerunt,& quibus proinde exlerte adscripserunt, in suis donationibus: in usus peregrinarum & pauperum.
