In omnibus Ita videmus, transactionem Passaviensem, de qua & supra, & pacis de religione decreta variorum in Imperio Comitiorum nunc etiam rata haberi, iterumque his nuperis tabulis confirmari: quodque de Augustana Confessione ibi dictum, Reformatos etiam comprehendit: quamvis alibi in Comitiis duarum religionum fit mentio, Augustan. a. 1555. Doch sollen alle andere, so obgemelten beyde Religionem nit anhangig in disem frieden nit gemeinc/ sonder gemeinlich auffgeschlossen seyn. Sic n. præterquâ in Comitiis de pace religionis Germanicis, quoque in Belgicis hoc intelligitur; in pace religionis, sub Archiduce Matthia facta a. clɔ lɔ lxxviii art. ii. libertas religionis decernitur duabus religionibus: quod anno seq. Pacificatione Coloniensi, art. xxi. Ordines explicatius dicunt libertatem religionis Reformatæ, atque Augustanæ Confessionis, una cum Romana. Confer etiam, si lubet, Goldasti Replicat. pro Imperio, cap. xl. & xli. Deniq; ex adductis apparet, nullam pacem Germaniæ haberi, nisi quæ etiam religionis certam pacem complectatur. Sed profecto bene est, quod pacis istius sagaces Arbitri, futuram ab Ecclesiastico (quem ex professione sua tamen omnium minime id decebat) adversus pacem, iniquam oppositionem protestationemq; prævidentes, illam tempestive re secaverint atq; rejecerint. Quæ autem illa pax Religionis sit, quæque compleCtatur, quæ Passavii primum a. clɔ lɔl i i initæ, Augustæ a. clɔ lɔ lv. & clɔ lɔ lxvi. atque post in diversis Imperii Comitiis, denique nuper Ofnabrugi confirmata, ut & Papa melius sciat, quid Religioni nostræ in Imperio jure debeatur, hocque & Imperator, aliiqué quorum interest semper probe teneant, ex ipsis Comitiorum Actis illa depromere ex re est. Primum ergo Augustæ Vindelicorum, in Comitiis a. clɔ lɔlv. postquam diu agitatum negotium pacificandæ utriusque religionis fuerat, saltem ad pacificam utriusque partis cohabitationem, & inturbatam publicam rem Imperii, convenit: nihil hostiliter ex religionis aliquo prætextu in alterum tentandum esse, sed liberum illius exercitium, & omnia jura intacta, bona quoque ecclesiastica à nostris occupata, in usus pios servanda impendenda, aliaque sive Ecclesiastico Ministerio, sive pauperibus attribuenda, citra discrimen religionis esse. §. 14. Setzen demnach / ordnen / wollen vnd gebieten / das hinfuro niemandts / was wurden / standts oder wesen der ley / vmb keinerley vrsachen willen / wie die namen haben möchten / auch in was gesuchtem schein das geschehe / den andern beuelchen / befriegen / berauben / faben / ober ziehen / belägern / vnd darzu für sich selbs / oder jemandt andern von seinet wegen nit dienen / noch einich Schloß / Stdtt / Marck / Befestigung / Dörffer / Höffe / vnd Weiler / abbrennen / oder ohn des andern willen / mit gewaltiger that / freuenlich einnemen oder gefährlich mit Brandt / oder in andere wege beschädigen / noch jemandts solchen Thätern rath / hülff / vnd kein ander weyß beyständt oder fürschub thun / auch sie wissentlich vnd gefahrlich nicht herberigen / behausen / ätzen / trencken / enthalten / oder gedulden / Sonder ein jeder den andern mit rechter freundschafft vnnd Christlicher lieb meinen / auch sein Standt noch gliedt des heyligen Reichs dem andern / So an gebürenden orten Recht leyden mag / den freyen zugang der Profiant / narung / gewerb / Rent / Güt / vnnd einkommen abstricken / noch aufhalten / Sondern in alle wege die Keyserliche Maiestat vnnd wir / alle Stände / vnnd hinwiederumb die Stände / die Keyserliche Majestat vns / auch ein Stand den andern bey diesem nachfolgenden Religions / auch gemeiner Constitution deß auffgerichten Landtfriedens alles inhalts bleibe lassen sollen. §. 15. Vnd damit solcher friede / auch der fraltigen Religion halbe wie auf hie vorermelten vnnd angetogenen vrsachen / die hohe notdurfft deß heyligen Reichs Teutscher Nation erfordert / dero beiderseits zwischen der Römischen Keiserlichen Majestat / vns / auch Churfürsten / Fürsten vnnd Ständen deß heiligen Reichs Teutscher Nation angeteilt / auffgericht / vnd erhalten werden möchten. So sollen die Keyserliche Majestat / wir / auch Churfürsten vnnde Stände deß heiligen Reichs / reinen stand deß Reichs / von wegen der Augspurgischen Confeßion / vnnd derselbigen lehr / Religion / vnnd glaubens halb / mit der that / gewaltiger weiß vberziehen / beschädigen / vergewaltigen / oder in andere wege / wieder sein Conscienz / gewissen vnnd willen / von dieser Augspurgischen Confeßions Religion / Glauben / Kirchen gebräuchen / ordnungen / vnd Ceremonien / so sie auffgericht / oder nachmals auffrichten möchten / in ihren Fürstenthumben / Landen / vnnd Herrschafften tringen / oder durch Mandat / oder in einicher anderer gestalt beschweren / oder verachten. Sonder den solcher Religion / Glauben / Kirchen gebräuchen / Ordnungen vnd Ceremonien / auch ihren Haab / Güteren / ligend vnnd fahrend / Landt / Leuthen / Herrschafften / Obrigkeiten / Herligkeiten vnd gerechtigkeiten / rüglich vnd friedlich bleiben lassen / vnd sol die Freyheit Religion nit anderth / dann durch Christliche / freundliche / friedliche / mittel vnnd wege / zu einhelligem Christlichem verstandt vnd vergleichung gebracht werden / alles bey Keyserlichen vnd Königlichen wurden / Fürstlichen ehren / waren worten / vnd Peen des Landtfriedens. §. 21. vnd sollen dannoch von solchen obgenanten Güttern / die Mot-turfftige Ministeria der Kirchen / Pfarrhen vnd Schulen auch die Almuffen vnd Hospitalia, die vormals bestelt vnd zubestellen schuldig / von solchen obgemelten Güttern / wie solche Ministerria der Kirchen / vnd Schulen vormals bestelt / auch nachmals bestelt / vnd versehen werden / vngeacht was Religon die seyen. Quae confirmata similiter in Comitiis Ra- tisbonensibus, a. cIↄ Iɔ Iɔ I I, & Augustan. a. cIↄ Iɔ I x. Vnd daß nicht desto weniger der Papstlich vertrag / auch der darauff erfolgt / vnnd allbie in fünff vnd funffzigsten Jbar beschlossen Religion vnd Landtfriede / sampt Handhabung vnd Execution derselbigen / für vnd für kräfftig vnd beständig bleiben. / Dero halben wir vns dann zu allen vnnd jeden Ständen / sampt vnd sonderlich versehen / setzen / ordnen vnd wollen / daß jergberührte / Pabst Paffauifche vertrag daraufferfolgte, vnnd albie im fünff vnd fünff iglien Jahr beschlossene Religion vnnd Landtsfriede / sampt Handthabung vnd Execution derselbige: steet / vest / vnnd vnverbrüchlich gehalten werden sollen. Alles bey den Versprüchnussen inn angeregtem Augspurgischen Abschied / weiter verbleibt vnd begriffen. Icerum in Augultanis, 2. cIↄ lxvi. ubi, post confirmata praecedencium hac in re Comitiorum edicta, ultra decernicur, oppresse propter religionem parti ferendas esse suppetias: Wir wollen auch vnser Thammergerichte vnd Beysszen vnsers Keys. Chammergerichts / hiemit abermals genedigkliches auferlegt / vnd befohlen haben / wie wir ihnen denn hiemit / trafft diefes Abschieds / auch außerlegen vnd verhelen / ob jemand / wer der were / wieder solchen Religion vnd gemeinen frieden beschwerdt were / oder fünfftiglichen beschwert vnd betrübt werden wolt / Daß auff der beschwerdten ahnrtiffen mit ertheilung gebürlicher rechtmeßigen hulff / sie sich fürderlich vnd gleichmessig e wenjen sollen. Wie wir dann als Römischer Keyser vnnd das Oberhaupt im Heiligen Reich / menglichen auch bey solchem Religion vnnd gemeinen frieden vnserm tragenden Keyserlichen Ampt gemeß su schügen vnd zu handthaben / so viel immer Menschlich vnnd möglich gerichte / auch urbütig nichts ermangeln / oder ahn vnserm gewesen / sorgfeltigem fleiß abgehen zu lassen / Damit ruhe / friede / einigkeit vnnd sicherheit im heiligen Reich erhalten / vnnd menniglichen bey dem seinigen gehandhabt werdem möge. Quæ ergo, qualisque illa religionis pax, in Imperio stabilita sit, utque solemniter ab Imperatore promissa, & Imperii Principibus Statibusque toties confirmata, quamque sub illis Protestantium religioni & causæ certum magnumque adversus oppressores debeat esse patrocinium, liquet. Scio nonnulla à Iesuitis, aliisque pacis inimicis adversus illas Pacificationes, præsertim adversus Passaviensem, oggeri, sed quæ quam vana sint, tum quanto Imperii totius, & Principum consensu, etiam ex multorum Theolog. Pontificiorū sententia, facteque illæ pacifications sint, vide quoq; apud Iohan. Gerhardi, in Confess. Cathol. lib. 1. cap. xix. (opere, quod (meo quidem judicio) in controversiis & disputationibus Pontificiis, multa nos omnes in scribendo levat opera). Iam verò opponat se Papa, ringatur rumpaturque, nobis in Imperatoris fide, & Imperii Comitiis, post Deum, satis præsidii, quoujque juri locus erit. Atque, quod ad pacem postremam Olnabrugensem, sic est, liberum ibidem religioni nostrę stabilitum exercitium, omni modo. Id est, quum libertas religionis sit vel conscientia, vel exercitii, & hujus aut privati in suis cuique domibus, vel publici, illa omnis pace nuperā in Imperio admissa, utinam modo servetur, & non tantum Papalis improba auctoritas & machinationes et-
units.tr: ...that those three religions shall be tolerated in the Empire. The more so, since it was well known that the chief causes of war had arisen from disagreements about religion. Therefore, if they loved peace (and peace is always to be preferred to war), they were bound to agree on this as the end and limit of the war: that, as had often been laid down by many earlier imperial decrees on the peace of religion, freedom and peace of religion should be kept whole and inviolate on both sides of each religion, with exact and mutual equality, as they now call it, and (as they well added) without regard to any opposition or protest against that peace, whether from the ecclesiastical or from the political side. These are the very words of the covenant: "Since in the present war a large part of the grievances which were in dispute between the electors, princes and estates of both religions gave cause and occasion, the following has been agreed and concluded concerning them. 1. The treaty concluded at Passau in the year 1552, and the peace of religion that followed it in 1555, as it was afterwards confirmed at Augsburg in 1566 and in various universal diets of the Holy Roman Empire, shall be held valid and shall be sacredly and inviolably observed in all its chapters, as agreed and concluded by the unanimous consent of the Emperor, the electors, princes and estates of both religions. But as to whatever has been decided in that treaty by the common agreement of the parties concerning some of the articles in controversy, these shall be observed as a perpetual declaration of the said peace, both in the courts and elsewhere, until by the grace of God agreement is reached on religion itself, and no contradiction or protest, whether from the ecclesiastical or the political side, made inside or outside the Empire at any time, is to be regarded; all such are declared void and of no account by virtue of these terms. In all other matters there shall be exact and mutual equality among all and each of the electors, princes and estates of both religions, so far as it accords with the form of the commonwealth, the constitutions of the Empire and the present agreement; so that what is just for one party shall be just for the other too. Violence of every kind and every act of force, as in other cases, so also here, is forever forbidden between either party." Add also §4, In omnibus. So we see that the Passau treaty, mentioned above, and the decrees of peace on religion of various diets of the Empire are now also held valid, and are confirmed again by these recent documents; and that what is said there about the Augsburg Confession also embraces the Reformed. Yet elsewhere at the diets mention is made of the two religions, Augsburg 1555: "But all others who do not adhere to the two religions named above shall not be included in this peace in common, but shall be expressly excluded." For thus it is understood not only at the German diets on the peace of religion, but also in the Belgian ones. In the peace of religion made under the Archduke Matthias in 1578, article 2, freedom of religion is decreed for the two religions; and in the following year, by the Pacification of Cologne, article 21, the States say more explicitly that freedom is granted to the Reformed religion and the Augsburg Confession along with the Roman. See also, if you wish, Goldast's Replicatio pro Imperio, chapters 40 and 41. Finally, from what has been adduced it appears that there is no peace for Germany unless it also embraces a sure peace in religion. But indeed it is well that the shrewd arbiters of that peace, foreseeing the unjust opposition and protest that would come from the ecclesiastical side (which, by its profession, least of all became it), cut it off in good time and rejected it. What that peace of religion is, and what it comprises, which was first concluded at Passau in 1552, confirmed at Augsburg in 1555 and 1566, and afterwards at various diets of the Empire, and finally recently confirmed at Osnabrück, it is useful to set out from the very Acts of the diets, so that the Pope may better know what is owed by law in the Empire to our religion, and so that the Emperor and others concerned may always thoroughly keep this in mind. First, then, at Augsburg in the diet of 1555, after the matter of pacifying both religions had been long debated, it was agreed at least for the peaceful coexistence of both parties and for the undisturbed public affairs of the Empire: that nothing is to be attempted hostilely against the other under any pretext of religion, but that its free exercise and all rights remain intact; that the ecclesiastical goods occupied by our side are to be kept and spent for pious uses, and that others are to be assigned either to the ecclesiastical ministry or to the poor, without distinction of religion. §14: "We therefore set down, ordain, wish and command that henceforth no one, of whatever rank, estate or condition, for no reason whatsoever, under whatever name or pretext it may be done, shall attack, make war upon, seize, plunder, or raid another, nor lay siege to any castle, town, market, fortification, village, court or hamlet, nor burn it, nor by violent deed or hostile force seize it without the other's consent, nor harm it by fire or in any other way; nor shall anyone give counsel, help, support or furtherance to such malefactors in any way, nor knowingly and dangerously lodge, house, feed, supply, harbour or tolerate them; but each shall deal with the other in true friendship and Christian love, and each estate and member of the Holy Empire shall allow the other free access to provisions, sustenance, trade, rents, goods and income, where legal right may be exercised, and shall not block or hinder them; but in all ways His Imperial Majesty and we, all the estates, and conversely the estates, His Imperial Majesty and we, and one estate another, shall let this follow and remain in force according to the content of this religious peace and the general constitution of the public peace that has been set up." §15: "And so that this peace, as well as the peace in the matter of religion, which, for the reasons mentioned above and cited, the high necessity of the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation requires, may be established and maintained, as it has been agreed between His Roman Imperial Majesty and us, and the electors, princes and estates of the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation, His Imperial Majesty, we, the electors and the estates of the Holy Empire shall not in deed, by violent means, attack, harm or otherwise oppress the estates of the Empire on account of the Augsburg Confession, its doctrine, religion and faith, nor against their conscience, will and mind compel them, in their principalities, lands and lordships, to abandon this Augsburg Confession, its religion, faith, church customs, ordinances and ceremonies, which they have set up or may hereafter set up, nor burden or despise them by mandate or in any other way; but they shall let them remain undisturbed and peacefully in such religion, faith, church customs, ordinances and ceremonies, and in their property, goods, both immovable and movable, land, people, lordships, authorities, dignities and rights; and the freedom of religion shall be brought to unanimous Christian understanding and agreement only by Christian, friendly, peaceful means and ways, all under the penalties of the Imperial and royal dignity, princely honour, word and the penalties of the public peace. §21: And from the said goods shall nevertheless be provided the necessary ministries of the churches, parishes and schools, and the alms and hospitals, which were formerly and are still obliged to be provided for; from the said goods, as the ministries of the churches and schools were formerly provided for and shall hereafter be provided and supplied, whatever religion they may be." This was likewise confirmed at the Regensburg diets in 1541 and at Augsburg in 1555. And so that the Papal treaty, and the one that followed it, and the religious and public peace concluded here in the fifty-fifth year, together with its enforcement and execution, may nevertheless remain effective and firm for ever, we therefore trust all the estates, together and each one, and so we set down, ordain and wish that the aforesaid treaty of Passau, and the religion and public peace concluded in the fifty-fifth year, with their enforcement and execution, shall be held firm, stable and inviolable. All this remains and is included in the promises made in the aforesaid Augsburg recess. Again at Augsburg, in 1566, where, after the confirmed edicts of the earlier diets on this matter, it was further decreed that aid should be given to a party oppressed on account of religion: "We also, through this recess, graciously lay upon and command again our Imperial Chamber Court and its assessors, as we do now by the force of this recess lay upon and command them, that if anyone, whoever he may be, should be harmed against such religion and the common peace, or should be grievously harmed and troubled, then upon the complaints of the injured, with the giving of due and lawful help, they shall proceed promptly and equally." Just as we, as Roman Emperor and head of the Holy Empire, are bound by our imperial office to protect and uphold such religion and the common peace, so far as human power and possibility allow, and we shall omit nothing ready or within our power, with careful zeal, so that peace, calm, unity and security may be kept in the Holy Empire, and each person may be upheld in what is his. What, then, and of what kind, the peace of religion established in the Empire is, and how solemnly it was promised by the Emperor and so often confirmed by the princes and estates of the Empire, and what sure and great protection it ought to be for the Protestant religion and cause against oppressors, is clear. I know that some things are alleged by the Jesuits and other enemies of peace against those pacifications, especially against the Passau one; but how empty these are, and how those pacifications were made with the consent of the whole Empire and its princes, and also by the opinion of many Papist theologians, see also in Johann Gerhard, Confessio Catholica, book 1, chapter 19 (a work which, in my own judgement, greatly lightens the labour of all of us in writing against Papist controversies and disputations). Now let the Pope set himself against it, rage and burst; for us, after God, there is enough protection in the Emperor's good faith and in the diets of the Empire, as long as there is place for law. And as for the last peace, that of Osnabrück: there, freedom of exercise of our religion is established in every way, that is, since freedom of religion is either of conscience or of exercise, and of the latter either private, in each one's own house, or public. Would that all of this, admitted into the Empire by the recent peace, were kept, and that the shameless authority and machinations of the Papacy did not bring it about that religion and peace are again overthrown together; for they are twin things, and as much as care or harm is done to religion, so much is done to peace. As to freedom of conscience the matter is plain, art. 5, §12. Moreover it was agreed that those Catholic subjects of ... of the Augsburg Confession...

units.la: Y ficiant, ut simul iterum religio & pax profligentur: gemina etenim illa sunt, & quantum religioni, tantum paci vel confulitur, vel officitur. De libertate conscientiæ res est manifesta, art. v. §. 12. Placuit porro ut illi Catholicorum subditi Augustanæ Confessioni addicti, ut & Catholici Augustanæ Confessionis statuum subditi, qui Anno millesimo sexcentesimo vicesimo quarto publicum vel etiam privatum Religionis suæ Exercitium ulla anni parte habuerunt, nec non qui post pacem publicatam, deinceps futuro tempore diversam à Territorii Domino Religionem profitebuntur, & amplectentur, patientur, & conscientia libera domi devotioni suæ, sine inquisitione aut turbatione, privatim vacare, in vicinia vero ubi & quoties voluerint, publico Religionis exercitio interesse, vel liberos suos exteris suæ Religionis scholis, aut privatis domi Præceptoribus instruendos committere non prohibeantur. Pro libertate exercitii, & primum privati, id est, quod in ædibus privatim intra domesticos parietes instituitur, ita enim hoc explicatur in ipsis articulis, art. iv. in causa Augustanæ Confessionis in Palatinatu: Caterisque id desiderauris Augustana Confessionis exercitium, tam publice in templis ad statas horas, quam privatim in ædibus proprijs, aut alienis ei res destinatis, per suos aut vicinos verbi divini Ministros peragere liberum esto. Pro illo privato (inquam) religionis nostræ per Imperium exercitio, est art. v. §. 12. Hoc tamen non obstante, Statuum Catholicorum Landsassii, Vasalli & Subditi cuiuscunque generis qui sive publicum sive privatum Augustanæ Confessionis exercitium Anno 1624. quacunque anni parte, sive certo pacto aut privilegio, sive longo usu, sive sola denique observantia dicti anni habuerunt, retineant id etiam imposterum una cum annexis, quatenus illa dicto anno exercuerunt, aut exercita fuisse probare poterunt. Quo ad publicum exercitium: licet istud frequentare in alieno territorio, uti ex allegatis modo apparet, & §. 13. ejusdem art. nobilibus Silesiis permittitur, ut Comites, Barones & Nobiles, illorumque in prædictis Silesia Ducatibus subditi, ob professionem Aug. Conf. loco an bonis cedere aut emigrare non teneantur, nec etiam prohibeantur dicta Conf. exercitium in locis vicinis extra territorium frequentare, modo in reliquis quis tranquille & pacifice vivant; seque tales praestent, quales erga suum summum Principem decet. Quin neque ob religionem nostros homines ulla in re postponendos esse, verum in juribus, beneficiis, officiis civilibus, & omnibus denique rebus juxta cum aliis habendos, decernitur, idque juxta veterum Comitiorum, ac pacis de religione sententiam, art. v. §. 12. Sive autem Catholici, sive Augustanae Confessionis fuerint subditi, nullibi ob Religionem despicatui habeantur, nec mercatorum, opificum, aut tribuum communione, haereditatibus, legatis, hospitalibus, leproforiis, eleemosynis, aliisve juribus aut commerciis, multo minus publicis caemeteriis, honorevesepulturae arceantur, aut quicquam pro exhibitione funeris a superstitibus exigatur, praeter cujusque Parochialis Ecclesiae jura, pro demortuis pendi solita, sed in his & similibus pari cum concivibus jure habeantur, aequali justitia protectioneque tuti. Secundum quam legem profecto haud decet, Protestantium religioni addictis, ob solam religionis causam jus civium in locis ubi ipsi & Parentes ipsorum nati, vi auferre, nisi pactis hisce aperte contraire, & jus illud quod natura dedit, infringere velimus: etenim cives origo facit. C. de Incol. l. 7. & D. ad municipal. l. 1. pr. & §. qui ex duobus. Hinc in Pacis articulo 111 statuitur, ut post universalis & illimitata amnestia fundamentum, omnes in eum utrimque statum restituantur in sacris & profanis, prout ante distinctionem gavisi sunt aut jure gaudere potuerunt, non obstantibus, sed annullatis quibuscunque interim in contrarium factis mutationibus. Et art. iv. quo ad personas & bona in eum vitae, famae, honoris, conscientiae libertatis Iuium & privilegiorum statum, quo ante dictos motus gavisi sunt aut jure gaudere potuerunt, utrinque restituuntur, nec eorum personis aut bonis ullum creator praejudicium, ullaveatio vel accusatio intentator, multo minus ulla poena, damnumve quocunque praetexu irrogator. Atque ita civium inter se pax & concordia tam quoad religionem, quam quoad politica firmata est. art. v.§.11. Neutrique partium alteram de Religionis sua exercitio, Ecclesia ritibus & caeremoniis disturbare fas sit, sed cives pacifice & comiter invicem cohabitent, liberumque Religionis sua & bonorum usum usum, ultro citroque habeant. Icq. insuper majoris concordia inter Status conservanda causa, cautum fuerit, quod nemo alienos subditos ad suam Religionem pertrahere eave causa in defensionem aut protectionem suscipere, illisve ulla ratione patrocinari debeat. Quare pax haec Germaniae non solum politica est, sed quoque religionis pax appellatur, in ipsis adeo articulis. art. v. §. 15. aliosque de religionis concordia tractatus anteriores confirmat, atque infractores illorum coercendos censet, §. 17. Utriusque Religionis Magistratus severe & rigorose prohibeat, ne quisquam publice privatimve concionando, docendo, disputando, scribendo, conjulendo, Transactionem Passaviensem, Pacem Religiosam, vel hanc imprimis sive declarationem, sive Transactionem ulpiam impugnet, dubiam faciat, aut assertiones contrarias inde deducere conetur. Quicquid etiam contrarii hactenus vel editum, vel promulgatum, publicatumve fuerit, irritum esto. Omnia quousque de religionis summa conveniatur, vel si hoc non fit, nihilominus pax religiose semper custodiatur. art. v. §. 1. donec per Dei gratiam de religione ipsa convenerit. §. 3. usquedum de religionis dissidiis per Dei gratiam conventum fuerit &c. Si vero quod Deus prohibeat, de Religionis dissidio amicabiliter conveniri non possit, nihilominus haec conventio perpetua sit & pax semper duratura. §. 9. donec controversia religionis amicabili partium compositione universali definiantur. & §. 12. 16. Hic autem habet Papa quod agat, si quid agendum sibi in communi hoc Christianismi negotio existimet, videlicet ut experiatur religionis inter partes hactenus adeo inimicas compositionem & concordiam. Frustra ego arbitror hic ab aliis multis laboratum esse, quandiu non ipse Papa huic operi accedit, & tum a se, tum de se illius exordium sumitur. Quid de Papismo loqueris aut concilando nobiscum, aut emendando, & hic multum molestiae facis tum tibi, tum aliis, donec ipsum Papismi caput & fundamentum. Papa videlicet, idem non agitat consilium, vel probat? donec ne hoc quidem annuit Papa, quod verum necessariumque, tum ad componenda religionis dissidia, tum ad orbis atque, que Imperii pacem judicant Imperatores, ut à persequendis propter religionem Protestantibus, vel vexandis iis abstineatur? Bene observavit in praefatione ad augustam temporis sui historiam Amplissimus Thuanus, Ferdinandum sapientissimum principem, postquam maxima ac periculosissima sub Carolo v. Fratre bella duxisset, experientia tandem didicisse, arma adversus Protestantes sumta hactenus male cessisse: quare & religionis pacem solenni decreto sancitam repetitis vicibus postea confirmarit. Unde Thuani, ad Regem Henricum iv. cui opus suum nuncupabat, ibi ingenua illa vox: bellum non esse legitimum modum tollendi ex Ecclesia scissurae. quae illa praefatione tractavit Auctor, ex voto, quo id futurum illius argumentum, si quando partem operis ederet, jam ante ab eo Casaubono significatum, hic refert epistola, quae inter epistolas Casauboni est cclvii. Fuit hic Thuanus ejusdem cum Cassandro, & Balduino, de religione sententiae, quo nomine illos dilaudat in illa sua praefatione, & lib. xxviii. in historia Colloquii Poissiacensi; & lib.xxxvi. ubi de excelsu Caesaris Ferdinandi: & Claudium Espencaeum, lib. L. Eo usque ei accedebat Casaubonus, ut, sed in Ecclesiae nostrae communione positus, solum cavenda extrema, diceret, sequendamque priscae Ecclesiae sententiam & consensum, in eoque figendos concordiae utrimque limites. Vide ejus praefationem in Polybium, & epist. ccxl. & civ. ccxxi. cclxiv. cccxvi. ccclxviii. units.tr: ...and that they do not also bring it about that religion and peace are overthrown together. For these two are twin concerns: as much as religion is promoted or harmed, so is peace. Regarding freedom of conscience the matter is plain: Art. V, §. 12. Furthermore, it has been agreed that those subjects of the Catholics who adhere to the Augsburg Confession, and likewise those subjects of the Catholic estates of the Augsburg Confession, who in the year one thousand six hundred and twenty-four had a public or even a private exercise of their religion at any part of the year, and also those who after the peace was proclaimed shall in future profess and embrace a religion different from that of the lord of the territory, shall suffer no hindrance, and shall be permitted to attend to their devotion freely in their conscience at home, privately, without investigation or disturbance; and in the neighbourhood, where and as often as they wish, to take part in the public exercise of their religion; nor shall they be forbidden to entrust their children to schools of their religion abroad, or to private tutors to be taught at home. As for the freedom of exercise, and first of the private exercise, that is, what is carried on privately within houses, behind domestic walls (for so it is explained in the articles themselves, Art. IV, in the matter of the Augsburg Confession in the Palatinate): Let it be free for the rest who desire the exercise of the Augsburg Confession to carry it on, both publicly in churches at the appointed hours, and privately in their own houses or in others set aside for such purposes, through their own or neighbouring ministers of the divine Word. For that private exercise of our religion (I say) throughout the Empire, there is Art. V, §. 12: Nevertheless, notwithstanding this, the landholders, vassals and subjects of every kind of the Catholic estates who in the year 1624, at whatever part of the year, had a public or private exercise of the Augsburg Confession, whether by a definite agreement or privilege, or by long use, or finally by mere observance of that year, shall retain it also hereafter together with its appendages, so far as they exercised it in that year or can prove that it was exercised. As to public exercise: although it is permitted to attend it in foreign territory, as appears from what has just been cited, and §. 13 of the same article permits the Silesian nobles, namely counts, barons and nobles, and their subjects in the aforesaid Duchies of Silesia, not to be bound to leave their place or goods on account of profession of the Augsburg Confession, nor to be forbidden to attend the said exercise of the Confession in neighbouring places outside the territory, provided that in other respects they live quietly and peaceably, and conduct themselves as befits them towards their own sovereign prince. Indeed it is also decreed that our people are not to be placed behind others in any matter on account of religion, but are to be held equal with the others in rights, benefits, civil offices and all things whatever, and this in accordance with the opinion of the old diets and of the peace concerning religion, Art. V, §. 12: Whether they be subjects of the Catholics or of the Augsburg Confession, they shall nowhere be held in contempt on account of religion, nor be excluded from the fellowship of merchants, craftsmen or tribes, from inheritances, legacies, hospitals, lazar-houses, alms, or other rights or commerce; much less from public cemeteries or the honour of burial; nor shall anything be exacted from the survivors for the performance of a funeral, beyond the dues of each parish church customarily paid for the dead; but in these and similar matters they shall be held with the same right as their fellow citizens, secured by equal justice and protection. Under that law it certainly does not befit us, to take away from those adhering to the Protestant religion, solely on account of religion, the rights of citizens in places where they themselves and their parents were born, by force, unless we wish to contradict these agreements openly and infringe that right which nature has given; for origin makes citizens (Cod. De incolis, l. 7; and Dig. Ad municipalem, l. 1 pr. and §. qui ex duobus). Hence in Article 111 of the Peace it is laid down that, after a universal and unlimited amnesty as the foundation, all are to be restored on each side in sacred and profane matters, just as they enjoyed or could have enjoyed their rights before the division, notwithstanding, and with annulled, whatever changes have been made in the meantime to the contrary. And Art. IV: As to persons and goods, all are restored on each side to their former state of life, reputation, honour, freedom of conscience, rights and privileges, which they enjoyed or could have enjoyed before the said disturbances; and no prejudice shall be done to their persons or goods, no action or accusation shall be brought, much less any penalty or damage inflicted under whatever pretext. And thus peace and concord among citizens themselves is confirmed, both as regards religion and as regards politics. Art. V, §. 11: Neither party may disturb the other in the exercise of its religion, its rites or ceremonies; but the citizens shall live together peaceably and courteously, and each shall have free use of his religion and his goods on both sides. And, moreover, for the preservation of greater concord among the estates, it has been provided that no one shall draw the subjects of others to his own religion, nor take them up for defence or protection on that account, nor in any way support them against their lords. Wherefore this peace of Germany is not only a political peace but is also called a peace of religion, in the very articles themselves: Art. V, §. 15, confirms the earlier agreements and treaties concerning concord in religion, and judges that their violators are to be restrained, §. 17: The magistrates of each religion shall severely and rigorously forbid anyone, publicly or privately, by preaching, teaching, disputing, writing or counselling, to attack the Treaty of Passau, the Religious Peace, or especially this declaration or transaction in any way, to make it doubtful, or to try to draw contrary assertions from it. Whatever contrary matter has hitherto been issued, promulgated or published shall be void. All these things hold until agreement is reached on the sum of religion; or if this does not happen, nevertheless the peace of religion shall always be kept. Art. V, §. 1: until by God's grace agreement is reached on religion itself; §. 3: until agreement is reached on the disputes of religion by God's grace, etc. But if, which God forbid, agreement on the dispute of religion cannot be reached amicably, nevertheless this agreement shall be perpetual and the peace shall always endure. §. 9: until the controversy of religion is settled by a universal amicable composition of the parties; and §§. 12, 16. Here the Pope has something to do, if he thinks anything ought to be done in this common business of Christendom, namely to try whether a composition and concord of religion can be reached between parties hitherto so hostile. I think that many others have laboured here in vain as long as the Pope himself does not join this work, and its beginning is not taken from him and from himself. Why do you speak of the Papists either agreeing with us or amending themselves, and why do you cause so much trouble for yourself and for others here, as long as the very head and foundation of Popery, namely the Pope himself, does not pursue the same plan or approve it? As long as the Pope does not even assent to this, which the emperors judge to be true and necessary both for settling the disputes of religion and for the peace of the world and of the Empire, that Protestants be refrained from persecution or vexation on account of religion? The most distinguished Thuanus well observed in the preface to his history of his own time that the most wise prince Ferdinand, after he had waged the greatest and most dangerous wars under his brother Charles V, had at last learned by experience that arms taken up against the Protestants had hitherto turned out badly; wherefore he afterwards repeatedly confirmed the peace of religion, sanctioned by a solemn decree. Hence in his preface to King Henry IV, to whom he dedicated his work, Thuanus uses that frank saying: war is not a lawful means of removing a schism from the Church. Which the author treated in that preface, in accordance with a wish he had already expressed earlier to Casaubon, which, if he ever published part of his work, would be its theme; this is related in a letter which is number 257 among the letters of Casaubon. This Thuanus was of the same opinion on religion as Cassander and Balduin, whom he praises by that name in that preface, and in book 28 in the history of the Colloquy of Poissy, and in book 36 where he speaks of the death of Caesar Ferdinand, and Claudius Espencaeus, book 50. Casaubon so far agreed with him that, though placed in communion with our Church, he said that only the extremes were to be avoided, and that the opinion and consensus of the ancient Church were to be followed, and that the limits of concord were to be fixed on both sides. See his preface to Polybius, and letters 240, 104, 221, 264, 316, 368. Moreover, how much these very men displeased the Papists is evident from various writings; and Rivetus, at the end of his Animadversions on Grotius's Cassander, proves this also from what he reports, that Casaubon's letters had recently been forbidden at Rome. Of this I want all to be certain, from the Bull itself which is in my possession, and which, since it is not open to all yet contains what it concerns many to know, we shall set out here, where we deal with the Bulls of the Popes. Decree of the Sacred Congregation of the most eminent and most reverend Lords, Cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, specially appointed by our most holy Lord Urban VIII, Pope, and by the Holy Apostolic See, for the Index of Books, and for the permission, prohibition, expurgation and printing of the same, to be published everywhere throughout the whole Christian Republic. I. Decree. The Sacred Congregation of the Index has judged that the books written below are to be published as condemned and prohibited, just as by the present decree it condemns and prohibits them, commanding everyone and each of whatever rank and condition, under the penalties contained in the Index of Prohibited Books, that none henceforth dare to print, read, or in any way keep them in his possession; and if anyone has any of them, he shall at once, from the notice of the present decree, hand them all over to the local ordinaries or to the inquisitors. The books are these: Antlia [ἀντλία], that is, a very full treatise on the right of asylum, by Georg Rittershausen, son of Conrad. Della Comunione con Iesu Christo nell' Eucharistia. Against the Cardinals Bellarmine and du Perron, a treatise by Jean Mestrezat, minister of the Word of God in the church of Paris, translated from the French into Italian by Vincenzo Paravicino, minister of the Word of God in the churches of Bondo and Castelegna in Bregaglia. Declaration of François Clouet, formerly called Père Basile of Rouen, in which he sets out the reasons he had for separating from the Roman Church to join the Reformed. Divina Sapientia, Arte construcła ad Cognitionem, & Amorem Dei acquirendum, by Johannes Blanco, Doctor of Medicine of Nice. Edonis Neuhusi Fatidica Sacra, or on the divine foretelling of future things, book II. The complete works of Johannes Cluverius. The letters of Isaac Casaubon, as many as could be found. Added is a letter on his illness and the causes of his illness, and an account of the same by Raphael Thorius. On the Royal Hand, a treatise by Gabriel Pereira de Castro. The Secretary of State of Monsieur de Silhon, translated from the French by Mutio Ziccarta. Paradisus Carmelitici Decoris, by Marco Antonio Alegere de Casanate. The Prince Nigello, by Guido Ubaldo Benamati. Proofs of the Liberties of the Gallican Church. Theologia Moralis by Étienne Bauny of Mosomum. By the same author: Somme des Péchez, which are committed in every estate. Practice of Canon Law. Storgae Salicec, that is, a letter in which an orthodox father tries to bring back a Papist son, by Stephanus Gabriel, minister of the church of Ilanz in the Grisons, of the Rhaetian league.
