Ille etiam Maximilianus præcipuus au‑ctor fuit primę inter Regias Belgarumqué, post Albani Ducis furias & devastationes, partes pacificationis tentatæ Bredæ a.cIↄ Iↄ Ixxv. missis eò legatis suis, Comitibus Swartzenburg & Hohenlo, ubi Ordinum Hollandiæ Selandiæque, & aliorum Confœderatorum nomine libertas Religionis inter præcipua capita habita fuit, demumqué a. cIↄ Iↄ Ixxv i. d. vi ii Novemb. inter Provinciarum Ordines, Gandavi conclusæ, quæ famosa illa & celebris fuit pacificatio Gandavensis: ubi art.v. edicta ante facta in causa hæresis suspenduntur, omniaqué quę exercitium religionis concernunt in Hollandia Selandiaqué; rejiciuntur ad generalem Ordinum conventum, art. iii. quo de Repub1ice negotiis communi suffragio statuatur. Quippe diligenter semper, quidquid sit de cæterarum in principio Provinciarum Ordinibus, Hollandiæ Selandiæque Ordines cautum voluere Religionis Reformatæ libertati & exercitio, cui illi aperte patrocinabantur, ita tamen ut in aliis articulis optime etiam convenirent cum reliquis Provinciis ad tutanda tum privilegia sua, tum ad expellendos Belgio Hispanos. Vnde Hollandiæ Ordines scripserunt ad Magistratum Amstelodamensem a. cIↄ Iↄ Ixxvi. d. xvii Decemb. quo eos ad se allicerent, in fœderis societatem: nil causæ esse ,,cur à se mutuo dissentirent, quin Hispanos censerent uti ,,& reliquæ Provinciæ omnes pro communibus Reipublicæ ,,hostibus, quos ab illis pro amicis haberi non credant. ,,Esse quidem discrimén aliquod inter ipsos de religione, sed ,,non illud debere eos in partes trahere circa politiam, li,,bertatum jura, & communis patriæ salutem. Ita palam discrimen hoc significant, atqué ab ipsis præstari patrocinium religioni Reformatæ. Quod vero in iisdem litteris additur: Or,,dines declarare, se ob causam religionis arma non sumsisse. Respondemus, id bene intelligendum esse de primi belli initiis, quod multa alia excitabant, præter religionem. Deinde, quod non solum, vel unice causa religionis in arma prorumpere Patres, imo nec illa potissima hactenus causa. Tertio, non ut religionem suam armis imperarent, vel conscientiis vim imponerent, uti Pontificii hactenus egerant: quare nunquam ,,nobis animus fuit quempiam vexare in conscientia sua, vel ,,ad nostram cogere religionem, absit. Quod autem etiam Religioni nostræ patrocinium, ubi illa agnita e turbis fuit, commodarint, hoc tempore, & his ipsis litteris satis apparuit, & quod anno sequente Harlemenses art. 1. proprium templum Religionis Reformatæ exercitio stipulati fuerunt, templum Mariæ in Bakenes: Quod Auriacus ejus promotionem, inter alios articulos Theod. Sonoio Northollandiæ Gubernatori a. cIↄ lↄ lxxii, imperarit: cui eidem quando testimonium sui ministerii perhibent Ordines a.cIↄ lɔlxxxviii ,,ajunt, Principem bellum adversus tyrannidem Hispani,,cam suscepisse pro defensione veræ, Christianæ, & Reformatæ religionis, atque pro defensione privilegiorum, ac libertatum patriæ. Omnes in id pariter convenicbant Ordines ac Provinciæ, ut patriæ jura defensum irent adversus externorum Hispanorum oppressionem, atque ut hos patria expellerent: Hollandiæ Selandiæque Ordines, & qui iiscum, cum Principe stabant, quoque Religionem Reformatam amplectise, defensam, promotamque velle significabant. adeo bene inter se conveniebant omnes, nisi quod alii ulterius pergentes, supra cæteros providi, Religionis quoque reformationem, una cum Patriæ illâ, jungendam censerent. Quod vides in Vnione Vltrajeċtina a. lↄ lↄ lxxix. art. xiii. addita ejus etiam explicatione. Iuxta quam Reformatis, eodem a.d.xv, Iunii, concessa quatuor in urbe nostra templa. Atque, sive in articulis cum Archiduce Matthia paċtis a. cIↄ lↄ lxxvii. art. xv. sive in plurimis aliis negotiis; & edicto Ordinum Generalium a. cIↄ lↄ lxxvi ii. & pace religionis, sub Archiduce erectâ Antverpiæ, a. cIↄ lↄ lxxviii. d. xxii. Iulii, qua & præcedentia Hispanorum de religione edicta tyrannica abolentur, & duabus religionibus, Reformatæ, ac Papisticæ pax mutua, suspensa omni in alteram vi armisque, dataque libertate quocumque locorum, ubi centum sint hujus aut illius religionis familiæ, exercitii ejus publici, art. II. III. IV. prohibita utrimque calumniandi alterum, vel incusandi leviter, aut lædendi famam nomenque, aliove quo pacto injuriandi licentia, art. XXIII. semper dico, & in quibuscumque negotiis imprimis pacificatio Gandavensis repetita, confirmata & ejus ratio habita fuit. Iamque Religionis Reformatæ professio & patrocinium Hollandiæ Selandiæq; communi Ordinum consilio concessa: quum præter id, satis adhuc causæ superesset, licet sacra Pontificia sequi volentibus, sive aliis, uniti ut permanerent pro patriæ bono ac salute, adversus Hispanos: uti in præfatione pacis-religionis loquuntur Ordines; & in litteris ad provincias Walonicas, a. MDLXXVIII. d. III. Martis: quæ Provinciæ hinc inter cætera ab Ordinibus deficiebant ac tumultuabantur, quod religionis Pontificiæ tenacissimæ, viderent Reformatam ubique magno applausu excipi & promoveri, sub Ordinum & Principis ductu, ac moderata Archiducis gubernatione: præsertim ofsensæ rebus Gandavensium, in propinquo acrius reformantium. Eandem religionis libertatem proposuerunt Ordines in pacificatione Coloniensi, art. XXI. a. MDLXXIX. Et Duci Alenconio, a. MDLXXX. d. XXIX Septemb. art. XII. XIII. observandam; de quibus quum in Deputatorum ex Ordinibus conventu Antverpiæ d. XII. Ianuarii, ejusdem anni ageretur, inter tria præcipua capita, propter quæ pugnatum hactenus sit, illud ponitur, ut iniqua persecutionum edicta tollerentur, ex adverso autem exercitium Reformatæ religionis, quod ad pacem & communem tranquillitatem necessarium existimabant, concederetur. Denique & hoc palam professi sunt Ordines Generales, in peremtorio illo quo Regem ejurarunt & deposuerunt edicto a. MDLXXXI. d. XXVI. Iulii. Nej jam dicam Ecclesiasticas Synodos hisce in regionibus jam tum aliquas ex consensu & authoritate publica DD. Ordinum habitas, quà provinciales, quà nationales. Præter Emdanam nationalem a. MDLXXXI. & ante eam Vesaliensis a. MDLXVIII. (cui inter plures alios subscripsit quidā Petrus ab Hoorn. Hoorenbeeckc) ad illam præparatoria: a. cIↄ Iↄ Ixxiv Provincialis prima publice habita Synodus fuit in Hollandia, Dordraci, primariâ Provinciæ istius urbeo: tum anno cIↄ Iↄ Ixxviii eadem in urbe, Synodus Nationalis, Ecclesiarum Belgicarum secunda, apud Hollandos prima: iterum Synodus Nationalis Medioburgi a.cIↄ Iↄ Ixxxi.d.xxix.Maji,quando ejusdem anni d.xxvi Iulii, Rex Hispaniæ publica authoritate imperio super hasce Provincias exuebatur. Vti quarta Nationalis post habita fuit Hagæ a. cIↄ Iↄ-Ixxxvi. Quę omnia eò faciunt, ut ostendam, quam necessarium omnino sit, Reformatæ religioni locum nusquam vel patrocinium occludi, quamvis etiā Papa vehementer reluctetur, atq; resistat. Bene est quod Politici omnes, quod Imperatores, Reges, Principes, & Respublicæ, in Imperio præsertim & Gallia, addo & Poloniâ, ubi Rex sub coronationem jurat conceptis verbis: pacem & tranquillitatem inter dissidentes de religione tuebor, ac manutenebo, quod primum Henricus Rex veteri juramenti formulæ addidit; quodq; in hoc nostro Belgio, à primis inde annis, optimum Proceres censuerunt atque ex salute esse Reipublicæ, ut libertas religionis Protestantibus largiatur, & sarta atque incolumis conservetur: nedum ut Romanus hic audiatur Papa, qui pro suo arbitrio, & proprio, id est pessimo motu pacem, & quæ ad eam stabiliendam facit, religionis libertatem condemnet.
units.tr: "But at Antwerp, thirteen thousand on one day and fourteen on another, and not long after sixteen thousand, were gathered. At Antwerp indeed, as he relates in the same book, sermons were never held with fewer than four thousand people. Those, of course, are the 'preaching men' whom he calls by that name elsewhere, book II and VI. In that same year the public preaching of the Reformed religion began in Belgium: from West Flanders, then through East Flanders, Brabant, Walloon territory, Gelderland, Friesland, Overijssel, Holland, Zeeland, and Utrecht as well. At first they preached in fields and open country, and because everywhere they feared violence and plots from the Papists, they were forced to carry arms with which to protect and defend themselves. At Antwerp, in June, they first asked for permission to preach outside the city, and then, on 3 July, by a humble petition, they asked for a place within the city to hold sermons, adding many serious reasons. As winter approached they obtained this. After the Governess had met with the nobles on 25 August (which Strada, like other things that seem to favour our side, omits, as a Jesuit and not with a historian's fidelity), article VI I, it was granted that wherever sermons were already being held, they might be permitted to continue, provided it was without arms and without scandal. In accordance with this, our sermons were openly permitted everywhere, in the towns too, wherever they had been held publicly on or before 25 August. At that time, and on what occasion, the Emperor Maximilian, an excellent prince of a very mild and prudent mind (who was the first to obtain freedom of religion for us here), replied to the King of Spain in September of this same year, 1566: that matters of religion were to be handled in no other way, both for himself in Germany and for the King in Belgium, than peacefully and gently by every means, not by force or arms; and that he offered his services and his name in that method, to act as mediator between the King and the people of Belgium, to settle the disturbances and dissensions that had arisen here. He wrote similar things the following year to the Governess Margaret; and finally he died while pursuing these very plans of pacification at the Diet of Regensburg in 1576. So necessary, the Pope knows, is it for the Reformed religion that its liberty and security be established everywhere. That same Maximilian was also the chief author of the first attempt at peace between the royal side and the Netherlanders, after the furies and devastations of the Duke of Alba, when he sent his envoys, the Counts Schwarzenberg and Hohenlohe, to Breda in 1575, where freedom of religion was treated among the principal heads, in the name of the Estates of Holland and Zeeland and of the other confederates. At last, in 1576, on 8 November, the Pacification of Ghent was concluded among the Estates of the Provinces, that famous and celebrated peace: where article v suspends the earlier edicts issued in the matter of heresy, and all matters concerning the exercise of religion in Holland and Zeeland are referred to the general assembly of the Estates, article iii, so that they may be decided by common vote on the affairs of the Commonwealth. Indeed, the Estates of Holland and Zeeland, whatever the Estates of the other provinces may have thought, have always carefully taken care, at the outset, for the liberty and practice of the Reformed religion, which they openly championed; yet in other articles they also agreed very well with the remaining provinces, both to protect their own privileges and to drive the Spaniards out of the Netherlands. Hence the Estates of Holland wrote to the magistrates of Amsterdam on 17 December 1576, to draw them into a league of alliance: there was no reason "why they should differ from one another, but that they should regard the Spaniards and all the other provinces as common enemies of the Commonwealth, whom they do not believe are to be counted as friends by them. There is indeed some difference between them over religion, but they ought not to drag that into matters of policy, the rights of liberties, and the common safety of the homeland." In this way they plainly signify this difference, and that protection is afforded by them to the Reformed religion. But what is added in the same letter, that the Estates declare they took up arms not for the sake of religion: we reply that this must be understood rightly, namely of the beginnings of the first war, which were stirred up by many other things besides religion. Next, it was not solely, or uniquely, for the sake of religion that the Fathers broke out into arms, nor indeed was that the chief cause hitherto. Third, they did not seek to impose their religion by arms, or to force consciences, as the Papists had hitherto done; therefore "it was never our intention to vex anyone in his conscience, or to compel anyone to our religion, God forbid." But that they gave protection to our religion as well, once it was recognized amid the disturbances, has been made sufficiently clear at this time and by these very letters; and also by the fact that in the following year the Haarlemers, by article 1, stipulated a church of their own for the exercise of the Reformed religion, the church of Mary in Bakenes; which William, among other articles, ordered for its promotion in 1572, to Theodore Sonoy, Governor of North Holland; and to whom, when the Estates bear witness to his ministry in 1588, they say that the Prince took up war against the tyranny of the Spaniards for the defence of the true, Christian and Reformed religion, and for the defence of the privileges and liberties of the homeland. All the Estates and Provinces agreed equally in this, that they would go forth to defend the rights of the homeland against the oppression of the foreign Spaniards, and drive them out of the country. The Estates of Holland and Zeeland, and those who stood with them and with the Prince, also signified that they wished the Reformed religion to be embraced, defended and promoted. All agreed so well among themselves, except that others, going further and being more far-sighted than the rest, thought that the reformation of religion ought to be joined with that of the homeland. You see this in the Union of Utrecht of 1579, article xiii, with its explanation added. By that, on 15 June of the same year, four churches in our city were granted to the Reformed. And whether in the articles agreed with Archduke Matthias in 1577, article xv, or in very many other matters; and in the edict of the General Estates of 1578, and in the religious peace established under the Archduke at Antwerp on 22 July 1578, by which the preceding tyrannical Spanish edicts on religion were abolished, and mutual peace was established between the two religions, the Reformed and the Papist, with force and arms against the other suspended, and freedom of public exercise of one or the other religion granted in whatever places there were a hundred families of this or that religion, articles II, III, IV; and mutual slander, light accusation, injury to reputation or name, or any other license to wrong, was forbidden on both sides, article XXIII; I say, in all these affairs, above all, the Pacification of Ghent was repeated, confirmed, and its principle observed. And now the profession and protection of the Reformed religion in Holland and Zeeland was granted by the common counsel of the Estates: since, beyond this, there was still enough reason, although those wishing to follow Papist rites or others were allowed to remain united for the good and safety of the homeland against the Spaniards, as the Estates say in the preface to the religious peace, and in their letter to the Walloon provinces of 3 March 1578. Those provinces were then revolting and rioting against the Estates, because they saw the most stubborn adherents of the Papist religion, Reformed religion being received and promoted everywhere with great applause, under the leadership of the Estates and the Prince, and under the moderate government of the Archduke; especially because they were offended by the affairs of the Ghent people, who were reforming more fiercely nearby. The Estates proposed the same freedom of religion in the Pacification of Cologne, article XXI, in 1579; and to the Duke of Alençon, in 1580, on 29 September, to be observed in articles XII and XIII. When these matters were being discussed at the meeting of the Deputies of the Estates at Antwerp on 12 January of the same year, among the three principal heads for which fighting had been carried on until then, this was set down: that the unjust edicts of persecution be removed, and on the other side that the exercise of the Reformed religion, which they judged necessary for peace and common tranquillity, be granted. Finally, the General Estates also openly professed this in that peremptory edict by which they renounced and deposed the King, on 26 July 1581. Now I shall not speak of the ecclesiastical synods already held in these regions with the consent and public authority of the Lords of the Estates, some provincial, some national: apart from the national synod at Emden in 1571 and, before it, the one at Wesel in 1568 (to which, among many others, a certain Peter à Hoorn, Hoornbeeck, subscribed), as preparation for that one; in 1574 the first provincial synod was publicly held in Holland, at Dordrecht, the chief city of that province; then in 1578 in the same city the national synod, the second of the Belgian Churches, the first among the Dutch; again the national synod at Middelburg on 29 May 1581, when on 26 July of the same year the King of Spain was stripped of rule over these provinces by public authority. Likewise the fourth national synod was held at The Hague in 1586. All these things serve to show how entirely necessary it is that no place or protection be closed to the Reformed religion, although the Pope strenuously resists and opposes it. It is well that all politicians, all emperors, kings, princes and commonwealths, especially in the Empire and in France, and I add in Poland, where the King swears at his coronation in express words: I will protect and maintain peace and tranquillity among those who dissent about religion, which King Henry first added to the old form of oath; and which, in this our Belgium, from the earliest years, the best nobles judged to be for the good of the Commonwealth, that liberty of religion be granted to Protestants and kept whole and inviolate: far less that this Roman Pope should be heard, who by his own judgment, and by his own motion, which is the worst kind, condemns peace, and the liberty of religion which serves to establish it."

units.la: Verùm, dicet hic fortasse aliquis, tu qui tam magnificè de pace religionis multa, & istum in finem profers pacta atque edicta Germaniæ, Galliæ, Belgii, vide ut illius quoque benè memor sis, quando in hoc ipso nunc Belgio Romana religio non jam amplius publico gaudet exercitio, sed verò ubique exterminatur. Vbi hic vel illa saltem pax, Reformatis prius indulta, nunc ipsis Romanensibus denegata & adempta? Resp. 1. Ante omnia distinguenda tempora, atque ex iis res & negotia, prout olim se habuere, vel hodie. Tres Reip. nostræ constituo periodos: prior continet originem & progressum motuum Belgicorum, ad a. cIↄ Iↄ Ixxxi. quo Regi milmissum palam repudium, idque juxta conditionem juramenti aRege sub inaugurationem praestiti: Et si nos aut ipsi, aut per alium quemvis, aut etiam haredes posterive nostri, contra hac aut universa aut singula, quocunque modo fecerimus: consentimus, volentesque animo permittimus iisdem nostris Pralatis, Baronibus, Equitibus, civitatibus, municipiis, omnibusque aliis nostris jam dictis subditis, ut nobis nostrisve haredibus aut posteris, nullum omnino obsequium praestent, neque in ulla re, qua nobis opus sit, quamve ab ipsis petemus aut requiremus, parebunt, donec quod ita committum fuerit, correxerimus, restituerimus, ab eoque plene desisterimus atque renunciaverimus. apud Agylaeum in Inaugurat. Philippi. pag. 148. Vt simili se sacramento Rex Poloniae, in coronatione sua, adstringit: si (quod absit) juramentum meum violavero, nullam nobis incolae regni obedientiam debebunt; sic me Deus adjuvet, & haec sancta Evangelia. Altera periodus est ab isto tempore bellorum ad a.cIo Io cxlvIII. initae utrimque pacis, hinc pacis temporal hodiernae; quam Deus felicem faciat, atque diuturnam. Primis temporibus libertas vel exercitium religionis Romanae inhibitum, non a Nostris fuit Reformationi addictis, sed ab ipsis suis Pontificiis Romanisque: ideo, quia sub indulto istius religionis exercitio frequentabantur vulgo conventus Hispanici, & pro horum tyrannide consilia. Sub illis se occultabant Religiosi quivis, qui in perniciem Reip. consultabant pro Hispanorum, adversus patriam ejusque jura & libertatem, molitionibus. Quare dum separari ab Hispanica factione tam difficulter vel omnino non possent coetus pro exercenda sua religione Papistici, interdicere illa & prohibere necesse duxere quotquot patriae, & pacis quam amantes, tam adversi Hispanis erant. Ita Amsterdami a.cIoIo lxxvIII, sequenti anno & iterum octagesimo, Antverpiae; quo eodem Bruxellis, & post alibi, factum. Dices, illa jam transiisse tempora, quibus Hispanorum nomen inimicum erat, pace facta hinc jam nihil timendum. At vero ego, quae hoc etiam tempore prudentia, & sagacitas requiratur in Proceribus, ne pacis dulce nomen socordes nos reddat securosque; nimium, quantopere vigilandum vel hoc quidem rerum statu maximè, providendumque sit, ut partam & singulari Dei munere concessam majestatem nobis posterisque integram tueamur, illorum, quorum hoc est, curæ committo. Liceat interim de Papistica illud hic usurpare, quod de hæresi, in oratione quadam Albani Ducis ponit Famianus Strada, lib. v i nunquam bona fide hæresim manjuefcere. Vel utut nulli incolarum nostrorum adversæ Religionis, Hispanice ultra animati sint, aut non id habeatur amplius argumentum diversarum partium, saltem Papæ Romano, vi religionis suæ, addicti & subjecti dum hi sunt, Reip. nostræ non potest non obesse habere subditos in alterius fidem juratos & ejus quidem qui in Ecclesiasticis non solum, sed & politicis ac corporalibus se omnium supremum, & Dei vicarium, & regnorum ac Rerump. Dominum habere jubet, quique pro suo arbitrio omnia moderetur, atque ex cujus nutu subditi fidelitatem suis Superioribus præstent aut negent, ipsique dominantes locum tanquam ab & sub ipso tenent denique suum, vel amittant. Hæc ut cum nullis bene constitutis Rebus p. ita minime omnium consistere cum nostra possunt, quæ Papæ non solum non obsequens ullo pacto, sed summo studio operaque adversatur, & propterea quoque execrationi est. Ac proinde quæ religio istis vinculis irretita est, subditosque alteri Monarchæ mancipatos habet, quam fovere minime debeat, neminiamplius poterit esse obscurum. Hinc a prin.is Reip. nostræ temporibus, non Hispanus tantum, sed & Papa, pro capitali hoste, à Proceribus nostris habitus fuit. In compositione tumultus hac in urbe a. cIↄ Iↄ lxxxi. excitati per Manipulares, ita primum edicitur: ut quicumque in concessu Ordinum ad futuri sint, teneantur renunciare Papæ, Regique Hispano, quippe ab Ordinibus Generalibus pro formatis & capitalibus habitis hostibus, juxta illorum decretum, nuper Amsterdami factum. Quis Papas Romanos nescit indefatigabili solertia semper subditos regiminis Reformati concitare & confirmare adversus suos Principes ac Magistratus? Exempla in Gallia, Anglia, Belgio minis crebra hic sunt & manifesta. Adhæc Iesuitismus, qui ab ipsis Romanæ religionis fautoribus pro intolerando bonis Rebusp. statu habetur, qui suis tum thesibus, tum studiis nil præter turbas moliuntur, & aliorum, qua Ecclesiasticorum juxta se, qua politicorum detrimentum ac ruinam, tum ipsorum suaeque minimæ Societatis sc. emolumenta & præcellentiam unice meditantur, eorumque dogmata ad unius Papæ nutum & dominium composita, in summorum capitū, Regum, Principumque perniciem conspirant, & à Politicis communi sensu conlensu pro exitiosis habentur, ille dico Iesuitismus quamdui cum vulgari Papismo tam arctam tenet communionem, ut separari vel nequeat, vel difficulter admodum possit, quis ægre feret nostros Magistratus adversus eundem tantundem tacere, pro conservando suo statu, ac sibi agendū judicant ipsi Papistici, qui multis variisque edictis, omnibus pene ditionibus Iesuitas sæpe exegerunt. Primi in nostris regionibus Antverpienses fuerunt a. cIↄ Iↄ Ixxvi i i. qui Iesuitas, quia juramentum fidelitatis Ordinibus, Archiduci, atque Araufionensi Principi, pro observanda Gandavensi pacificatione, detrectabant, clamantes se Papæ Romano jurasse, sua urbe expulerunt. mox Brugenses, eodem anno, d. vi i i Augusti; quum illud Antverpiæ factum esset d.xvi i i. Maji. Inde singularia adversus eos Ordinum Generalium edicta, quibus fœderato Belgio excluduntur. a. cIↄ Iↄxcvi. & cIↄ Iↄc xi i.cIↄ Iↄ cxvi i. post expiratas duodecennes inducias: quo decreto Ordines dicunt damnosam & truculentam Iesuitarum sectam, qui præter idololatriam quam docent, etiam subditos ab obedientiâ abducunt, & ad patrandas Principum & Magnatum cædes instigant, proditiones ad promovendam tyrannidem Hispanicam & Papalem moliuntur, cœtus Reip. pernitiosos instituunt, aliaque quæ ne agant, ipsis omnino prospiciendum fit. Quę aliis postmodum edictis repetiverunt, atque confirmarunt iterum a. cIↄ Iↄc xxix. & cIↄ Iↄc xli.& nuper. Videri illa possunt in Codice Edictorum DD. Ordinum, part. i. pag. 179. 435. part. ii. pag. 184. & alibi. Atque ob eaidem causas jam à multo tempore exaɗi fuerunt iidem ex Gallia, Angliâ, Venetiis, Bohemiâ, aliisq; orbis Christiani partibus. E Gallia quidem a. cIↄ Iↄ xcIv.d.xxIx Decembris. quod confirmatum denuo a. cIↄ Iↄ xcvII. d.xxI. Augusti, & sequenti a. cIↄ Iↄ xcvIII. d. xvIII. Augusti. Burdegalâ a. cIↄ Iↄ lxxxIx. Vide Thuanum sub finem lib.xcIv. Ex Angliâ, primum sub Elizabetha. a. cIↄ Iↄ lxxx r. tum Iacobo R. a.cIↄ Iↄ cvI. quod edictum exhibet in Historia sua Baudartius, lib. xII. Venetiis exacti fuerunt a. cIↄ IↄcvI. quod decretum apud eos renovatum a.cIↄ Iↄc xII.quatenus prohibebetur, ne etiam liberi Venetorum ad illorum Scholas mittantur instruendi: atque denuo a. cIↄ Iↄ cxxII. Genuâ, a. cIↄ Iↄ cIv. edicto, uti ajunt, perpetuo & irrevocabili. Bohemia, a. cIↄ IↄcxvIII.d. II Iunii. ubi Directores Rerum Bohemicarum dicunt, Iesuitas solos causam fuisse omnium tumultuum, & calamitatum, quæ illis obvenerint. Moravià, anno seq. cIↄ Iↄcx Ix. d.vI Maji. Hungaria, eodem tempore, d.xvI. Maji. ne alia dicam. Quibus addere licet epistolam Christiani Saxoniæ, Electoris, ad Matthiam Archiducem a. cIↄ Iↄ cvIII. d. vI. Octobris scriptam, in Iesuitas omnem causam distractionum & tumultuum per Imperium, & vere quidem, rejicientis. Quotquot unquam Reges, Principes, Status illos suis ditionibus exterminarunt, causas ejus facti politicas attulere, quod homines sint turbulenti, & truculenti, gnari solummodo factiones, dissidia, cædes bellaq; concitare, Papæ perniciosa mancipia, ei qui subjicere omnia, & sub ejus nomine sibi ipsis satagunt, in quæ finem summis Principibus aliquando & vitam, & regimen quantū in ipsis, auferant. Cujus rei manifestum satis argumentum est, quod vel conspirationum, vel cædium auctores, in maxima capita ab aliquo tempore destinatarum, in Regina, Regesque Angliæ, Galliæ, Principes nostros, prodiere omnes ex Schola Iesuiticâ, eo videlicet homines deducentibus Iesuitarum non studiis solum, ut vitia duntaxat hominum haberi possint, sed ipsis dogmatibus, quod in variis egregiisque in Iesuitarum causa
units.tr: But perhaps someone will say here: you who speak so grandly of the peace of religion, and bring forward so many treaties and edicts of Germany, France and Belgium to that end, see that you also remember this, since in this very Belgium the Roman religion no longer enjoys public exercise but is everywhere driven out. Where now is that peace, or at least that one, granted earlier to the Reformed and now denied and taken away from the Romanists themselves? Answer. 1. Above all, the times must be distinguished, and the affairs and transactions according as they stood formerly or today. I mark three periods in our Commonwealth. The first contains the origin and progress of the Belgian disturbances, down to the year 1581, when the open repudiation was sent to the King, in accordance with the condition of the oath sworn to the King at his inauguration: And if we, or anyone else on our behalf, or even our heirs and successors, act against these things, whether all or any of them, in any way whatsoever: we agree, and by our will grant to the same our Prelates, Barons, Knights, cities, towns, and all our other aforesaid subjects, that they shall render to us or our heirs or successors no obedience at all, nor shall they obey in any matter in which we need their service, or which we shall ask or require of them, until what has been so committed shall have been corrected and restored, and we have fully desisted from it and renounced it. Cited from Aggelaeus in the Inauguration of Philip, p. 148. Likewise the King of Poland binds himself by a similar oath at his coronation: If (which God forbid) I shall violate my oath, the inhabitants of the kingdom shall owe us no obedience; so may God help me, and these holy Gospels. The second period runs from that time of wars to the peace begun on both sides in 1648, and hence to the present peace, which may God make happy and lasting. In the early times the free exercise of the Roman religion was forbidden not by those of us committed to the Reformation but by the Papists and Romanists themselves. This was because, under the license of the exercise of that religion, meetings of Spanish men were commonly held, and plans were made for their tyranny. Under cover of these, any religious men who plotted to the ruin of the Commonwealth were hiding, working for the Spaniards against the fatherland, its laws and its liberty. Therefore, since the Papist assemblies could not be separated from the Spanish faction so easily, or not at all, those who loved their country and peace, and were as hostile to the Spaniards, thought it necessary to forbid and prohibit them. So it was done at Amsterdam in 1578, the following year and again in 1580 at Antwerp; the same was done at Brussels in the same year, and afterwards elsewhere. You will say that those times are now past, when the name of the Spaniards was hostile, and that since peace has been made there is nothing more to fear. But I, who think that even at this time prudence and sagacity are required in the nobles, lest the sweet name of peace make us careless and secure, commit to those whose duty it is the care of preserving intact the majesty we possess, granted by a singular gift of God, for ourselves and our posterity, and I say how greatly we must be watchful, and especially in the present state of affairs, and take care. Let me meanwhile here borrow what Famianus Strada, in a certain speech of the Duke of Alba, book 6, says of heresy: never to tame heresy in good faith. Even if none of our inhabitants of the opposing religion are any longer animated towards Spain, or this is no longer regarded as a sign of opposing parties, nonetheless those who are bound and subject to the Roman Pope by the force of their religion cannot fail to harm our Commonwealth, while they have subjects sworn to another's faith. That prince claims for himself the supreme place in ecclesiastical matters, and also in political and temporal ones, as the Lord of all, the vicar of God, and the Lord of kingdoms and commonwealths; he governs all things at his own will, and at his nod his subjects give or withhold fidelity to their superiors, and those who rule hold their place as from him and under him, and finally either keep or lose it. Since these things cannot be reconciled with any well-ordered commonwealth, much less with ours, which is not only in no way obedient to the Pope but opposes him with the greatest zeal and effort, and is therefore also an object of execration, it will by no means be unclear to anyone which religion is entangled in these bonds and holds its subjects bound to another monarch, and which religion ought in no way to be fostered. Hence from the beginnings of our Commonwealth not only the Spaniard but also the Pope was regarded by our nobles as a capital enemy. In the settlement of the tumult raised in this city in 1581 by the Manipulares, it was first ordered that whoever is to be admitted to the assembly of the Estates must renounce the Pope and the King of Spain, as enemies judged by the General Estates to be sworn and capital, according to their recent decree at Amsterdam. Who does not know that the Roman Popes, with untiring skill, have always stirred up and confirmed their subjects against the princes and magistrates of the reformed government? Examples in France, England and Belgium are here abundant and manifest. Besides, Jesuitism, which is held by the very supporters of the Roman religion to be an intolerable state for good commonwealths, plots nothing but disturbances with its theses and its studies, and aims solely at the harm and ruin of others, both ecclesiastical and political, beside itself, and at the advantage and pre-eminence of itself and its very small Society; and its doctrines, framed to the nod and dominion of one Pope alone, conspire to the destruction of the chief heads, kings and princes; and they are held to be pernicious by politicians with common consent. That Jesuitism, I say, so long as it keeps such close communion with common Papism that it cannot be separated, or only with great difficulty, who would not be annoyed that our magistrates are silent against it, when the Papists themselves judge that it is their own business to preserve their state? They have often expelled the Jesuits from almost all their dominions by many and various edicts. The first in our regions were the men of Antwerp in 1578, who, because the Jesuits refused the oath of fidelity to the Estates, the Archduke and the Prince of Orange, for observing the Pacification of Ghent, shouting that they had sworn to the Roman Pope, drove them from their city. Soon after, the men of Bruges, in the same year, on 8 August, after the same had been done at Antwerp on 18 May. Then came singular edicts of the General Estates against them, by which they are excluded from the united Belgium, in 1596, 1612 and 1616, after the twelve years' truce had expired. By this decree the Estates call the Jesuit sect harmful and savage, who, besides the idolatry they teach, also lead subjects away from obedience and incite them to carry out the murders of princes and magnates, and plot betrayals to advance Spanish and Papal tyranny, and set up pernicious meetings against the Commonwealth, and other things, against which provision must absolutely be made. These the Estates later repeated and confirmed again in 1629, 1641 and recently. These can be seen in the Code of the Edicts of the Lords of the Estates, part 1, pp. 179, 435; part 2, p. 184, and elsewhere. And for the same causes the same men have long since been expelled from France, England, Venice, Bohemia and other parts of the Christian world. From France indeed, in 1594, on 29 December, which was confirmed again in 1597, on 21 August, and the following year, 1598, on 18 August. At Bordeaux in 1589; see Thuanus near the end of book 94. From England: first under Elizabeth in 1580, then under King James in 1606, which edict Baudartius presents in his History, book 12. At Venice they were expelled in 1606, and that decree was renewed among them in 1612, in so far as it was prohibited that even the children of the Venetians be sent to their schools for instruction; and again in 1622. At Genoa in 1604, by an edict, as they say, perpetual and irrevocable. In Bohemia in 1618, on 2 June, where the Directors of Bohemian affairs say that the Jesuits alone were the cause of all the tumults and calamities that befell them. In Moravia in the following year, 1619, on 6 May; in Hungary at the same time, on 16 May. To say nothing of others. To these may be added the letter of Christian, Elector of Saxony, written to the Archduke Matthias in 1608, on 6 October, which casts upon the Jesuits the whole cause of the divisions and tumults throughout the Empire, and truly so. Whatever kings, princes or states have ever driven them out of their dominions have given political reasons for the act, namely that these men are turbulent and savage, knowing only how to stir up factions, dissensions, murders and wars, pernicious tools of the Pope, who strive to subject everything to him and, under his name, to take for themselves, so far as in them lies, at last the life and government even of the highest princes. A sufficiently clear proof of this is that the authors of conspiracies or murders, directed for some time against the chief heads, against the Queen and the kings of England and France, and against our princes, all came out of the Jesuit school; for the study of the Jesuits leads men, not merely so that they may be regarded as vices of individuals, but by their very doctrines, as in various and excellent writings in the cause of the Jesuits

units.la: causa actionibus ostendere Parisienses, tum Scholæ Doctores, tum Advocati juris, quorum ad a. clɔ lɔ xciv. & clɔ lɔ cxi historiæ ubertim meminerunt. Hinc Rex Galliæ Henricus iv. in orat. ad Parlamentum habita a.clɔ lɔ xcixd.xvi. Februarii, quamvis Papistam se, noluit autem Iesuitam profiteri, sed distinxit: catholicus sum, catholicus Rex, Romanus Catholicus, non catholicus Iesuita. Quocirca quum Papilmus vulgariter, & saltem in nostris partibus, ita totus Iesuitismo delibutus & intertextus sit, ut ab eo occupetur atque regatur, præsertim quando ab ipsis Papistis non repellitur violenter arceturque, sed in veneratione est, summo jure quin factum sit nullus negabit, quod non illam Papistis hic concedant Proceres nostri libertatem, quam cupiant & velint, adeo (ne de Ecclesia, hominumque æterna salute dicam) Rebulp. pernitiosam. Lubet hic usurpare, & nostra facere verba Hieronymi Vendrameni, Controversf. Venet. i. pag.13. crescunt singulis pene diebus nova religiosorum familia, Veneto nomini infestos fautores habent, Venetæ ditionis provincias, urbes, Castella percurrant, Venetis itaq; non timendum, præsertim si prope arces vel mænia, hujusmodi templa[?] vel domos ædificent? sciunt quid faciunt Veneti, nec enim sine causa suas leges condunt. Ipsos appello hic Venetos, immo Ordines Monachales omnes, annon quod Resp. Veneta tum dixit, majori jure & causa queant dicere adeoque debeant, pro suis ditionibus, Provinciarum nostrarum Illustrissimi Ordines? Insuper quando propius doctrinæ Papisticæ introspicitur genius, multa eam habere, quæ regimini nostro ejusque quieti directe adversantur in tyrannnidem nata, deprehendemus. Quis latis unquam dixerit, quanto odio hæreticos, quos appellant, nos videlicet, quos hæreticorum primos pessimosque æstimant, prosequuntur, istudque Reipublicæ nostræ regimen, quod religione, ut basi nititur, totumque se pro illa conservanda, & defendenda promovendaque lubens impendit, exceretur. Unde continuo adversus nos precantur, vota faciunt, indulgentias hoc fine concedunt, quemadmodum solenne in indulgentiarum diplomatibus pro haresium extirpatione, ac S. Matris Ecclesia exaltatione; consilia quævis capiunt, ad nos invadendos, opprimendos, extirpandos. Cujus rei affatim adsunt præter exemplorum hodiernorum, apud nos, vicinasque nationes regnaque, & priscorum, etiam doctrinæ documenta, quà quod agunt, docent etiam a: que defendunt, quinimo extollunt, eo usq; ut Divorum & Martyrum Catalogo adscribant Principum Regumq; parricidas. Ne extera dicam, Principis nostri fcelcratus occisor Balthafar Gerardus, merito cum Ioanne Nicomedien si martyre comparandus, dicitur Arnoldo Rayssio, in Hierogazophylacio Belgico, pag. 187. & Guiljelmus Eftius, præterquam quod facinus idem laudat, in Historia Martyrum Gorcomiensium, cap. VI. libellum de istius martyrio: le glorieux & triomphant Martyre de Balthasar Girard, sua commendatione approbavit: de quo alibi plura diximus. Nec aliud S. Inquisitionis argumentum est vel negotium, quam nostræ religionis homines omnes ferro flammaque excindere & extirpare, cujus vim, si qui alii, nostri sane hisce in regionibus satis olim experti sunt. Et ne alia dicam, quæ huc innumera adferri possent, quid aliud Gaspar Scioppius, tum in Consilio Regio, ad Hispaniæ Regem; tum in Classico belli sacri, uti ipse libri titulum præscribit ad Imperatorem, agit, quam ut primo loco doceat, nos hæreticos omnes eradicandos esse? hæretici & scismatici statim interficiendi, inquit cap. 11. sui Classici. Cap. 111. Alterius religionis homines Christianorum neque Reges, neque judices esse possunt. Scelus est hæreticum imperare Catholicis, taliaque plura axiomata, nonnili ad sacces ubivis orbi subjiciendas, ad bella, strages, & confusionem rerum omnium ruinamque inducendam nata, Consiliarius Regis, ac Imperatoris scilicet, & Theologus, ex doctrinæ suæ Papisticæ penu producit & jactat; breviter, nos omnes Amalekitarum instar, occidendos esse. Quod à Pio v. discere potuit, qui a. tlo lo lxix in epist. ad Carolum Gallię Regem, eodem propósito exemplo, Sauli Regis adversus Amalekitas, trucidandos extinguendosque per universum ejus regnum nostros homines, diligenter Regem monebat. In quam sententiam milites Papæ istius Pii v. in Galliam mittendos cohortatus est Possevinus, lib.{l} il Soldato Christiano, eorum officii esse ut omnes Protestantes occidant, alioqui eos & fidem & salutem amissuros. Atque postea qui scripsit, sub regnum Henrici iv Navarrei, Guiljelmus Rossæus librum, sane flammis infernalibus expiandum, de iusta Reip. Christiana in Reges impios & hæreticos auctoritate; iustissimaque Catholicorum ad Henricum Navarrænum, & quemcunque hæreticum à regno Galliæ repellendum consederatione. proh, quæ ibi impia, horrenda, adversus religionis nostræ homines, ecclesiam nostram, Reges, principes, Resp. ocurrunt, plenis modis trimodiisque ceu ex barathro effusa, eaque ex sententia, & doctrina Ecclesiæ Romanæ! hodiernam hæresim, maximè Calvinia am quæ in Galliâ serpit, esse Saracenismo vel Paganismo longe detestabiliorem: propte-reaque longe magis esse Christianis rationibus utile, ut Paganus aliquis, vel Saracenus, vel Turca, quam ut Calvinstia Galliæ rex præficiatur. Ibidem in præfatione, ubi libri sui summam proponit: Qui etiamsi esset, loquitur de Navarræo, in solio Regali constitutus, generalique Francorum assensu & approbatione rex admissus; si tamen in hæresim incideret, eamque pertinaciter defenderet, ut in potestate est non modo Pontificis Ecclesiæ summi, sed etiam Gallicani regni episcoporum, eum deponere & Regia dignitate privare; ita talis Ecclesiæ sententia justissimè armat non solum reges exteros sed etiam suos ipsius domesticos subjectos, ut sana integraque conscientia eum & possint & etiam debeant impugnare, ejusque à se dominatum & jugum rejicere, nec unquam ad talis hæretici regis obedientiam revertere. Vides, quæ sit istius Ecclesiæ indoles adversus generalem Francorum assensum, & approbationem, & Regiam Majestatem, subditos armare, incitare, ad Regem impugnandum dejiciendumque. Hinc illa libri sui habet capite primum septimo, nos nimirum esse Gentiles, Ethnicos, Judæos; imo Gentilibus & Judais longe nequiores: quin Calvinstam esse inter alios omnes hæreticos tanto magis pernitiosum, quanto cancer aut pestis inter morbos, quanto inter serpentes reliquorum princeps ille reregulus vel basiliscus, qui ipsos etiam serpentes inficit. Tum, de Rege Navarreno Galliis praficiendo: Tu regno Gallia, populo Christiano, regem dabis non Anglum, non Burgundum, non Hispanum, quod iege Salica interdictum putas, & recte; non Turcam, non Saracenum, qui Christianos in suis Imperiis patiuntur vivere, sed Calvinistam Turca & Saraceno longe nequiorem. Et ne dubites hanc haberi Ecclesiae apud illos sententiam, subjungit: quod si quis Ecclesiasticam vocem audire desideràt, & cum Imperatoria jure & sententia, Pontificale item jus judiciumque conjungi postulat, noverit id Ecclesia non minus quam Imperii principes semper in hoc conspirasse, semperque de haereticis tanquam de maxime perniciosis Christianismi hostibus ex Christiana repub. exterminandis diligentissime elaborasse, adeoque nihilo minori quam Imperatores & vehementia & solicitudine, civiles honores officiaque haereticis quibuscumque interdixisse. Alii enim superiorum Pontificum documenta sequentes, statuunt ne haeretici, credentes illis, receptatores, defensores, & fautores eorum, ipsorumque filii, usque ad secundam generationem ad aliquod beneficium Ecclesiasticum seu publicum officium admittantur: quod si secus actum fuerit, sit irritum & inane. haec ex vi. Decret. lib. v. tit. ii. cap. Statutum, & cap. Quicunque. Addit: Alii haereticos bovis omnibus evertendos esse decernunt, suaque decreti rationem firmam ex jure civili, & ex theologia quoque sanctiori afferunt. Alii juri divino & Evangelii Christi regulis innitentes, ostendunt obedientiam subditorum cum haeresi non posse consistere, sed illam ab ista tanquam contrariam a contrario, ut frigus a calore, ut lucem a tenebris expelli.
units.tr: The Parisians show this by their actions, both the doctors of the University and the lawyers, whom the histories of 1594 and 1611 mention at length. Hence King Henry IV of France, in a speech to Parliament delivered on 16 February 1599, although he was willing to be called a Papist, refused to profess himself a Jesuit, and drew this distinction: I am a Catholic, a Catholic king, a Roman Catholic, not a Jesuit Catholic. Since, therefore, Papistry in general, and at least in our parts, is so steeped in and interwoven with Jesuitism that it is governed and controlled by it, especially when the Papists themselves are not violently repelled or kept out but are held in honour, no one will deny, with the strongest right, that our nobles grant the Papists here a liberty which they desire and wish for, one that is (not to speak of the Church and the eternal salvation of men) very harmful to the commonwealth. It is fitting here to borrow and make our own the words of Girolamo Vendramin, Controversiae Venetae i, p. 13: New religious families grow almost every day; they have supporters hostile to the name of Venice; they run through the provinces, towns and fortresses of the Venetian dominion. Shall the Venetians then not fear, especially if these men build temples or houses near their citadels or walls? The Venetians know what they are doing, nor do they make their laws without cause. I call here upon the Venetians, or rather all the monastic orders: should not our illustrious orders, for their own dominions and provinces, be able to say, and indeed ought to say, with greater right and reason what the Venetian Republic then said? Moreover, when we look more closely at the character of Papist doctrine, we find that it has many features that are directly opposed to our government and its peace, features born for tyranny. Who could ever say with what hatred they pursue heretics, as they call us, whom they judge the first and worst of heretics, and how they curse that government of ours which rests upon religion as its foundation and gladly devotes itself wholly to preserving, defending and advancing it? Hence they pray against us continuously, make vows, grant indulgences for this purpose, as is customary in indulgence documents for the extirpation of heresies and the exaltation of Holy Mother Church; they adopt every plan to invade, oppress and exterminate us. Of this there is abundant evidence, besides present examples among us and in neighbouring nations and kingdoms, and the teachings of ancient doctrine as well: what they do, they also teach, and what they teach, they defend, and indeed exalt, to the point of enrolling among the saints and martyrs the murderers of princes and kings. To say nothing of other cases, the wicked slayer of our Prince, Balthasar Gerard, deserves to be compared with John of Nicomedia as a martyr, according to Arnold Raissius in the Hierogazophylacium Belgicum, p. 187; and Guilielmus Estius, apart from praising the same deed in his History of the Martyrs of Gorkum, chapter VI, approved by his own commendation a little book on that man's martyrdom, le glorieux & triomphant Martyre de Balthasar Girard; about which we have said more elsewhere. Nor is there any other object or business of the Holy Inquisition than to cut off and root out with sword and fire all men of our religion, a power which some of our people, certainly in these regions, have long since experienced well enough. And, to pass over the countless other instances that could be brought forward here, what else does Gaspar Scioppius do, both in his Consilium Regium, addressed to the King of Spain, and in his Classicum belli sacri, addressed to the Emperor, as the title of the book itself indicates, than first teach that all of us heretics must be eradicated? Heretics and schismatics are to be killed at once, he says in chapter 11 of his Classicum. In chapter 111: Men of another religion cannot be kings or judges of Christians. It is a crime for a heretic to rule over Catholics, and many similar axioms, born only to subject the peoples of the world everywhere, to induce wars, slaughter, confusion of all things and ruin: these the king's counsellor, or rather the emperor's, and theologian, produces and flaunts from the storehouse of his Papist doctrine. In short, all of us are to be killed like the Amalekites. He could have learned this from Pius V, who in 1569, in a letter to Charles, King of France, urged the king carefully, with the same purpose and the example of King Saul against the Amalekites, to slaughter and exterminate our men throughout his whole kingdom. To the same effect Possevino exhorted the soldiers of this Pope Pius V to be sent into France, in his book Il Soldato Cristiano: it was their duty to kill all Protestants, otherwise they would lose both their faith and their salvation. And afterwards, under the reign of Henry IV of Navarre, William Rossaeus, a book surely to be expiated with infernal flames, wrote On the just authority of the Christian commonwealth against impious and heretical kings, and on the most just league of the Catholics to repel Henry of Navarre and any heretic from the kingdom of France. Alas, what impious and horrible things there meet us against the men of our religion, our Church, kings, princes and commonwealth, poured out in full and triple measure as if from an abyss, and that by the judgement and doctrine of the Roman Church! The present heresy, especially the Calvinist one that creeps through France, is far more detestable than Saracenism or paganism; therefore it is far more useful to Christian interests that some pagan, or Saracen, or Turk should be set over France than that a Calvinist should be. In the same book, in the preface, where he sets out the sum of his work, he says of the Navarrese: Even if he were, let us say, placed on the royal throne and admitted as king by the general assent and approval of the French, yet if he should fall into heresy and obstinately defend it, then, since it lies within the power not only of the supreme Pontiff of the Church but also of the bishops of the Gallican kingdom, to depose him and strip him of royal dignity, such a sentence of the Church most justly arms not only foreign kings but also his own domestic subjects, so that with a sound and whole conscience they both can and ought to attack him, and to reject his rule and yoke, and never return to obedience to such a heretical king. You see what the character of that Church is: to arm and incite subjects against the general assent and approval of the French and against the royal majesty, to attack and depose the king. Hence in the seventh chapter of the first book of his work he has: that we are, of course, Gentiles, heathens, Jews; indeed far more wicked than Gentiles and Jews; and that the Calvinist is more pernicious than all other heretics, as cancer or plague is among diseases, as that prince of serpents, the basilisk or cockatrice, which infects even the serpents themselves, is among the rest. Then, about setting the King of Navarre over France: you will give the kingdom of France, the Christian people, a king who is not English, not Burgundian, not Spanish (which you think is forbidden by the Salic law, and rightly so), not Turk, not Saracen, who allow Christians to live in their empires, but a Calvinist, far more wicked than Turk or Saracen. And lest you doubt that this is the Church's opinion among them, he adds: if anyone desires to hear the Church's voice, and asks that the Pontifical right and judgement be joined with the imperial law and sentence, let him know that the Church, no less than the princes of the Empire, has always been of one mind in this, and has always laboured most diligently to banish heretics, as the most pernicious enemies of Christianity, from the Christian commonwealth; and so, with no less vehemence and anxiety than the emperors, it has forbidden civil honours and offices to heretics of every kind. For other Pontiffs, following the precedents of their predecessors, have decreed that heretics, believers in them, receivers, defenders and favourers of them, and their sons, are not to be admitted, down to the second generation, to any ecclesiastical benefice or public office; and if it has been done otherwise, let it be void and of no effect. These things are from the sixth book of the Decretals, title 2, chapters Statutum and Quicunque. He adds: others decree that heretics are to be overthrown by every means, and they support their decree with firm arguments from the civil law and from the more sacred theology as well. Others, relying on divine law and the rules of the Gospel of Christ, show that the obedience of subjects cannot coexist with heresy, but that the one must be driven out by the other as its contrary by its contrary, as cold is driven out by heat and light by darkness.

units.la: Capitis octavi argumentum est: Rex haereticus per Pontifices justè excommunicari, & jure Regio aliuqui debito privari potest, quam ait sententiam esse sine omni quaestione à Christianis recipiendam, ut vere Christianus haberi non possit, si quis Ecclesiae sententiam agnoscens, de ea in posterum disputare aut litigare voluerit. Capite nono probare intendit: quod Contra regem haereticum recte pieque non modo à regibus Christianis, sed etiam à suis ipsius subditis bellum potest suscipi. Regi haeretico obedientia non debetur. At vero quantam illa sonant tyrannidem, quamque evertunt omnem Rempublicam, & ejus nezum? Ecclesiæ, sacerdotique deferre judicium in Reges & regna, subditosque si Ecclesiastico, si Papæ videatur, ad obedientiam nullam erga Magistratus suos teneri: manifestum est, inquit idem pag. 612. regem lepra hæresíque infectum, é regesiers privatum, populíque fidelis officium quod Deo & Ecclesiæ debetur postulare, ut quem regem sacerdos propter lepram hareticam eiecit ex Ecclesia, eundem ipsum resp. non aliter quam privatum quemvis hominem legibus obnoxium exterminet é civili societate. Hinc ergo judicium fiat, an male dicamus, cavendam nostris Rebusp. esse religionem Romanam, ejusque publicum patrocinium, propter ejus seditiosa, & tyrannica axiomata. Ne nunc alia ejusdem commatis scripta adducam, similiaque inde facile themata, ex Bellarmino, contra Barclayum de potestate Papæ, Becano, Mariana de Institutione Principis, quorum libri Parisiis ideoque combusti fuere. Et Scioppium quod attinet, ejusque sacrum Classicum, quo omnes Reges & Principes adversus Protestantes incitare & accendere satagit, nihilque quam rerum omnium miserrimam conturbationem & stragem intendit, à cervicibus Protestantium in Germania quidem inchoandam, verùm quam non inultum ferrent Auctores, si Sciopianis consiliis ad talia facinora instigari & protrudi se paterentur, ille, (dico) Sciopius, bonorum malitix, & pessimorum hominum decus, nam in Iesuitas utcumque ferventissimus, ab illis tamen etiam inter probatos pro fide Pontificia Scriptores recensetur, à Becano, in prasat. ad Tom. III. Opusc. Theolog. digne exceptus, & obtusum effractumque ejus Classicum, mox ac auditum, à variis fuit, inter quos Iustus Mejerus I.c. Argentoratensis, in Scripto eleganti & docto, adversus Sciopium, super illo Sciopii in libris principali argumento: Sintne Protestantes jure Cæsareo hæretici, & ultimo supplicio afficiendi? ubi Author ex professo & accurate exponit præter alias Iuris Civilis leges, eas quæ de hæreticis loquuntur C. de summa Trinitate, & de Hæreticis & Manichæis. præter alia eruditi commatis, quæ immiscet. Sed & Tubam Pacis occinuit eidem Sciopiâno Classico Theodosius Berenicus, Noricus, æmulo Taciti stylo, monitisque ex eodem historico, aliisque creberrime intertextis, data opera, uti in præfatione exponit, quia Scioppius Tacitum suo judicio valde depretiarat. Quare & rei, & styli causa optimus, qui legatur, liber ille est, quo Auctor ex tribus præcipue causis refellit Classicum Scioppii, quod bellum ejusmodi sacrum nec utile, nec honestum, neque facile futurum esset, aliisque multis argumentis Papalia istiusmodi consilia pro dignitate exagitat & revincit. Non omittere possum quod utrumque, Mejerus ille, & Berenicus, quorum ille Argentorati, a. cIↄ Iↄ cxxiii. hic Augustæ Trebocorum scripsit, anno sequente, Scioppio quam bene applicant proverbium istud Italicum, de Germano Italiæ incubante: Todesco Italianato, Diavolo incarnato; Germanus Italicus, Diabolus incarnatus. Ne quod Mejerus pag. 4. refert, addam Scioppium Venetiis aliquando in carcerem compactum fuisse, ob improbum quoddam consilium quod Diabolus Monacho cuidam mago suggessisset, & ab hoc accepisset ipse: ut non mirum, qui tali utitur hominum Diabolorumque commercio, non alia spirare quam truculenta & Diabolica consilia norit. Hæc hactenus. Neq; jam dixi, quod primo quidem loco ponendum fuerat, ut quum propter multiplicem idololatriam Papistica religio merito nobis abominanda sit, pro ossicio id agere debere Proceres, ea ut, secundum Dei voluntatem, terra nostra quantum possit maxime, expurgetur. Ob quod minus sedulo à Regibus sive Iudaicis, sive Israeliticis curatum sæpe Deus gravia adversum illos pronunciavit exhibuitque judicia. Quare videndum etiam atque etiam venit, ne nobis exprobretur id, quod tum Pergamensi Ecclesiæ Apoc. ii. 14. Christus dicere jussit: sed habeo adversum te pauca, quod habeas illic qui tenent doctrinam Balaam, qui docebat Balacum objicere offendiculum coram filiis Israelis ut ederent ex iis, quæ simulacris erant immolata, & ut fornicarentur. tum Thyatirensi, vers. 20. sed habeo adversus te pauca: quod permittis mulierem Iezabel, quæ se dicit Prophetissam, docere & seducere servos memeos, ut scortentur, & edant ex iis quae simulacris immolantur. Praeterquam quod id salutari Ecclesiarum à Papatus corruptelis Reformationi debeamus etiam, ut hanc omnia pacto promoveamus in terris nostris, & commendemus apud alios, quo latius se indies exporrigat, atque animas Christo lucretur ac veritati. Non enim gratum nobis aliter opus ac beneficium Reformationis ostendimus, nisi apud omnes quoque eandem pro virili prosequamur, atque eacum quae pugnant omni studio emendare studeamus & corrigere. Et erunt Reges nutritii tui, & feminae principes eorum nutrices tuae. Iesa. xlix. 23.
units.tr: The argument of the eighth chapter is that a heretical king can justly be excommunicated by the Popes and deprived of his royal right and other dues. The author says this opinion is to be accepted by Christians without any question, so that no one who acknowledges the Church's sentence could be considered a true Christian if he wished to dispute or contend about it afterwards. The ninth chapter aims to prove that war may be rightly and piously waged against a heretical king, not only by Christian kings but also by his own subjects. Obedience is not owed to a heretical king. But how much tyranny these words imply, and how completely they overturn every commonwealth and its well-being! They would hand judgment over kings and kingdoms to the Church and the priesthood, and would have subjects, if the ecclesiastical authority or the Pope thinks fit, owe no obedience at all to their magistrates. "It is plain," says the same author on page 612, "that a king infected with leprosy and heresy, and deprived of his kingdom, makes the faithful people's duty, which is owed to God and the Church, a demand that the commonwealth should banish him from civil society in no other way than any private man subject to the laws, whom the priest has cast out of the Church on account of his heretical leprosy." Let judgment therefore be passed on whether we speak falsely when we say that the Roman religion, and its public patronage, must be guarded against in our commonwealth because of its seditious and tyrannical maxims. I will not now cite other writings of the same kind, or similar themes that are easily drawn from them: from Bellarmine against Barclay on the power of the Pope, from Becanus, and from Mariana on the instruction of a prince, whose books were therefore burnt at Paris. As for Scioppius and his "Sacred Trumpet Call," with which he labours to stir up and inflame all kings and princes against the Protestants, and which aims at nothing but the most wretched confusion and slaughter of all things, to be begun against the necks of the Protestants in Germany, yet authors would not bear it without retaliation if they allowed themselves to be incited and urged to such crimes by Scioppian counsels. That Scioppius (I say), the glory of the wicked and the shame of evil men, who is extremely fervent against the Jesuits, is nevertheless counted among the writers approved by them for the Papist faith; he was worthily taken to task by Becanus in the preface to the third volume of his theological tracts. And his "Trumpet Call," as soon as it was heard, was blunted and broken by various writers, among whom is Justus Meyer of Strasbourg, in an elegant and learned writing against Scioppius on that chief question of Scioppius's book: "Are the Protestants heretics under Caesarean law, and to be punished with the last penalty?" In it the author expounds, expressly and accurately, besides other laws of civil law, those laws which speak of heretics, in the Code under "On the Most Holy Trinity" and "On Heretics and Manichaeans," together with other learned remarks which he interposes. But Theodore Berenicus of Nuremberg also sounded a Trumpet of Peace against that same Scioppian Trumpet Call, in a style that rivals Tacitus, and with admonitions drawn very frequently from that historian and woven in on purpose, as he explains in his preface, because Scioppius in his judgment had greatly belittled Tacitus. So for both the subject and the style, that book is an excellent one to read, in which the author, for three chief reasons, refutes Scioppius's Trumpet Call, showing that a war of this kind would be neither holy, nor useful, nor honourable, nor easy to bring about; and with many other arguments he thoroughly exposes and overturns such Papal counsels as they deserve. I cannot omit that both Meyer and Berenicus, of whom the former wrote at Strasbourg in 1623 and the latter at Augsburg in the following year, aptly apply to Scioppius that Italian proverb about the German brooding over Italy: "A German made Italian is a devil incarnate; a German Italianized is the Devil incarnate." Not to add what Meyer relates on page 4, that Scioppius was once thrown into prison at Venice on account of a wicked plot which the Devil had suggested to a certain monk who practised magic, and which he himself had received from him: it is no wonder that one who deals in such commerce with men and devils knows how to breathe nothing but savage and devilish counsels. So much for these matters for now. I have not yet said what should have been put first: since the Papist religion, on account of its manifold idolatry, is rightly abominable to us, it is the duty of the nobles to see to it that our land, as far as possible, is cleansed according to the will of God. For God has often pronounced and carried out grave judgments against kings, both Jewish and Israelite, because they had not taken this care diligently enough. Therefore we must consider again and again lest there be thrown in our faces what Christ ordered to be said to the church at Pergamum, Rev. ii. 14: "But I have a few things against you, because you have there those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the children of Israel, so that they might eat things sacrificed to idols and commit fornication." And to the church at Thyatira, v. 20: "But I have this against you: that you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants, so that they commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols." Apart from this, we owe it to the Reformation for the salutary cleansing of the Churches from the corruptions of Popery that we promote all these things in our lands in every way, and recommend them to others, so that it may spread more widely day by day and win souls for Christ and for the truth. For we do not show the work and benefit of the Reformation as welcome to us unless we also pursue the same with all our strength among all others, and strive to amend and correct the things which oppose it with all zeal. "And kings shall be your nursing fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers." Isa. xlix. 23.

units.la: Quapropter multis gravissimisque rationibus adducuntur Proceres nostri, quod Papisticae religioni non majorem indulgent libertatem, adeo, praeterquam animis multiplici sua superstitione, idololatria, & erroribus, Reip. quoque ob perniciosas molitiones, tum Papae Romani auctoritatem, Iesuitica axiomata & studia, denique doctrinae omnimodam tyrannidem, spiritualem ac corporalem, summe exitiosae. Frustraque est vel qui integram illis libertatem poscat, quam nec illi, qui iisdem sacris quamvis favent, sed politicae magis gnari sunt, his in locis expetant, non liberum publicumque Religionis ipsorum exercitium, sed domesticum duntaxat, editorumque adversus eos intermissionem aliquam Galliae Legatus praeses Ianinus pro illis petitum veniebat, ab Ordinibus post expiratas cum Hispano inducias a. cIↄ Iↄ cıx. idemque a. cIↄ Iↄ clxliv. Comes Avauxius, cum Serviento, & Cogneto de la Thuillerie: vel qui hoc qualecunque pro iis jam tentet, sciat frustraneum esse totum super hac re consilium, nisi primo prospectum Magistratui nostro sit, de non fota per ipsos hinc idololatria, de securitate à molitionibus adversus Rēpublicam, & de abjurato prius palā Papa Romano tanquam supremo eorum domino, tum ut Iesuitica factio expellatur, & tyrannis à doctrina Papistica segregetur, denique & Nostri in illorum terris & dominiis ea gaudeant felicitate, quam illi apud nos ambiunt: quemadmodum Iohanni Austriaco, petenti templa Pontificiis in Hollandia, Selandiaque responsum ab Ordinibus meminit Hubertus Languetus, in epist.a. 1577. ad Camerarium : Ioannes ab Austria petiit ab Hollandis & Zela. dic ut in quolibet oppidorum quae obtinent, commundant templum unum Pontificiis: quod promiserunt se fasturos m[?]pse idem praestet iis qui secum in religione sentiunt in Provinciis illis, in quas habet imperium. neque enim ex jure amplius possunt Papistae pro se apud nos agere, ut satis bene scivere, qui aliquando pro illis apud Illustriss. DD. Ordines intercessere Galliae Legati; sed ex sola gratia & favore obtinere debent quod sperent, jure omni olim, vitio ac perduellione sua privati, aut sponte exuti, & supremâ Ordinum auctoritate, in quam negotium hoc omne in variis pacificationibus semper rejectum, resita prout ex salute publica, ordinante, nihil illi ultra nunc habent quod dicant, dum omne ex arbitrio dependet & potestate DD. Ordinum suprema & autocratorica. Conferas in hanc rem volo etiam dissertationem Celeberrimi nostri Voetii, super quaestione: An sedes Romana sit compatibilis cum Politiis Reformatis; tum, an Theologi dicam, an Iurisconsultimajoris, quique quam omnigena scientiarum suppellectile in rebus & disputationibus Theologicis deceat nos instructos esse, suo exemplo docet, Guljelmi Prynn Angli librum, ex Anglico in Latinum conversu à Wolfgango Meyero Theologo Basileensi, Fulmen tum gladii Christianorum Regum, Principum, & Magistratuum; ubi adversus hodiernos in Anglia Independentes, praecipue Wilhelmum Dillum, cujus concione in hanc litem prodigus est, probat ex Scriptura, legibus, & rationibus variis, authoritatem & potestatem Magistratus in coercendis & puniendis, pro criminis gravitate, idololatris, haereticis &c. cum responsione, quod vel hic maxime attenditur, ad contrarias exceptiones & argumenta.
units.tr: For this reason our nobles are urged, on many very weighty grounds, not to grant the Papist religion greater liberty. For apart from the souls it harms by its manifold superstition, idolatry, and errors, it is also most deadly to the commonwealth because of its pernicious schemes, namely the authority of the Roman Pope, Jesuit maxims and practices, and finally its total tyranny over doctrine, both spiritual and bodily. And it is vain to demand full liberty for them; nor, in these places, should those who favour the same rites but are more versed in politics than in religion seek for them not a free and public exercise of their religion, but only a private one, and some suspension of the edicts against them. This the French ambassador, the president Jeannin, came to ask on their behalf from the States after the truce with Spain had expired, in 1609; and the same was asked in 1644 by Count d'Avaux, together with Servient and Cogneth de la Thuillerie. Whoever now attempts even this sort of thing for them should know that the whole plan in this matter is futile, unless first provision is made for our magistracy: that there be no secret idolatry from them here, security against their schemes against the commonwealth, and that they first openly renounce the Roman Pope as their supreme lord; then that the Jesuit faction be expelled, that tyranny be separated from Papist doctrine, and finally that our people in their lands and dominions enjoy the same happiness that they seek among us. Thus Hubert Languet, in his letter to Camerarius of 1577, records the answer given by the States to John of Austria, who asked the Hollanders and Zeelanders for churches for Papists: "John of Austria asked the Hollanders and Zeelanders that in each town they hold, they should grant one church to the Papists; they promised that they would do this, provided that he himself grants the same to those who agree with them in religion in those provinces over which he has rule." For the Papists cannot, as a matter of right, plead anything further on their own behalf among us; as the French ambassadors, who at times interceded for them before the most illustrious Lords States, have known well enough. Rather, they must obtain by favour and grace alone what they hope for, since they were long ago deprived by right, through their own fault and treason, or had put it off of their own accord, and the matter, which in the various pacifications has always been referred to the supreme authority of the Lords States, is so ordered by that authority as the public welfare requires. They now have nothing more to say, since everything depends on the will and the supreme and absolute power of the Lords States. I also wish you to consult on this matter the dissertation of our most celebrated Voetius, on the question: "Whether the Roman See is compatible with Reformed polities." Further, whether I should call him a theologian or a jurist of the greater sort, who by his own example teaches what kind of learning, with all its varied furnishings, it becomes us to have in theological matters and disputations, is William Prynne's English book, translated from English into Latin by Wolfgang Meyer, a Basel theologian, The Thunderbolt of the Sword of Christian Kings, Princes, and Magistrates. In it, against the present-day Independents in England, especially William Dell, whose sermon he takes up in this dispute at great length, he proves from Scripture, laws, and various reasons the authority and power of the magistrate in restraining and punishing, according to the gravity of the crime, idolaters, heretics, and so on; with a reply to the opposing objections and arguments, to which, above all, the closest attention is paid here.

units.la: §.xiii. Hactenus illa examinavimus in Bulla Papae, quae adversus Pice Germanig adfert, tu ex bonis Ecclesiasticis (horum enim primae & potissima à Papis semper habetur ratio, quasi religionis Papalis anima) à Protestantibus possessis; tu ex libertate religionis in Imperio confirmata, indeque Protestantium jux-ta ta cum aliis ad publica munia & officia admissione; sequitur querela ejus ab amissis suis inde reditibus, & jure vel usurpatione in Ecclesias Germaniæ relcissa: Annata, inquit, jura Pallii, Confirmationis, Menses Papales, & hujusmodi jura ac Reservationes in bonis Ecclesiasticis dicta Confessionis Augustanæ ecluduntur. Resp. Quæ hic taxat Papa, continentur art. v. Pacis Germanicæ, §. iv. jura eligendi & postulandi juxta cujusque loci consuetudines & statuta antiqua, illibata maneant, quatenus illa Imperii Constitutionibus, Transactioni Passaviensi, Paci Religiosæ & imprimis huic declarationi & transactioni sunt conformia & intuitu Archiepiscopatuum Augustanæ Confessioni addictis permanentium ea nihil inse continent illi Consessioni adversum, Et §. v. Si quid annatarum, larium Palli, confirmationum, Mensium Papalium, & hujusmodi jurium & reservationum nomine in bonis Statuum Augustanæ Confessionis Ecclesiasticis immediatis à quocunque, quandocunque aut quomodocunque prætendatur, id validitate & executione à brachio seculari impertienda careat. Duo Papa, qui istis obloquitur, hic committit crimina. Primum, quod illa ceu jura sibi arrogat; alterum, quod ista servata sibi cupit etiam in bonis Protestantium, vel hinc exclusa dolet: quorum hoc ridiculum & ineptum satis est, illud etiam improbum. Primo enim quod Annatas concernit, quod iterum non ad usum Ecclesiæ, sed ad bona pertinet, sunt illæ fructus primi anni ex vacante beneficio Papæ pendendi; instituti primitus vel commenti ab eo ex specie saratione pro inferendo Turcis bello quasi sacro, sed quâ occasione ille usus tantummodo fuit in suum ipsius commodum, ut sub hoc prætextu magnam numorum ex hominibus emungeret copiam, & perpetuo gauderet inde tributo. Annatarum initium refertur ad Iohannem xxii. cui pro tempore illæ concessæ fuere, ex aliis dignitatibus & beneficiis, exceptis abbatiis, pro bello ultra mare adversus Turcas incundo: alii ad Bonifacium ix. referunt, Theodoricus à Niem, qui à Secretis ei fuit; Stella: cupidus augenda Ecclesiastica dignitatis, primus Ecclesiasticis beneficiis cis ctis anatharum usum imposuit : hac feiliget conditione, ut qui beneficium consequeretur, dimidii anni proventus Apostolicæ Camera pelsolveret. Idem & Platina; qui addit: Sunt tamen qui hoc inventum Ioanni xxii adscribant. Hanc autem consuetudinem omnes admisere praeter Anglos qui id de solis Episcopatibus concesserunt, in ca-teris beneficiis non adep. Deinde alii Pontifices similes aliquando instituerunt exactiones, expressis certis causis; illaque clerus, Principes & populi tolerarunt aliquando, quandoque etiam recusarunt: quod in Anglis, alibique factum. De vacantibus vero beneficiis, & fructibus primi anni majorum praelaturarum, abbatialium, & episcopalium nullum aliud initium perhibetur, quam voluntaria & gratuita oblatio quorundam, qui in discordia electi ad abbatiales vel cathedralem ecclesiam, appellantes ad Romanam curiam, illo modo superiores evaserant & confirmabantur. Initio quotiescumque vacare contigisset beneficium, etiamsi plus quam semel in anno, à beneficiatis novæ exigebantur annatæ: & quoties vacabant (etiam si ter aut pluries vacassent in anno) pro qualibet mutatione tituli voluerunt habere & exigere fructus & primi anni beneficii, sive praelatura vacantia, & aliquando longe ultra, & quandoque Papa qualibet vice Annatas vacantes habebat, & Cardinales nihilominus partem mediam, quodq; propter vacan. fuerunt quandoque privati praelati & translati invitis, & quandoque propter plus offerre (sumptis aliis coloribus) assumpti & alii praelati, qui forte non fuerunt praeferendi, ex quibus sequuta sunt strages, guerra, scandala etiam nondum sopita, inquit, qui de Annatis non solvendis, tempore Constantiensis Concilii, ab hujus ista in re decreto appellationem instituit, & nomine Ecclesiæ Gallicanæ scripsit Nicolaus Clemanges, quod editum primo fuit ab Orthunio Gratio, in fasciculo Rerum expetendarum; inde à Ioh. Martino Lydio, cum Operibus Clemangis: qui in fine tractatus istius exhibet etiam formulas obligationis pro Annatis. Sed in Concordatis Nationis Germanicæ a. cIↄ cccxlvii. cum Gregorio xiii. illud eatenus accilum est, ut nec de omnibus beneficiis solvendæ fuerint annatæ, non de minoribus, neque illæ nimiæ aut statum Ecclesiæ prægravantes, nec de omnibus Ecclesiis aut locis, & nisi semel, quamvis etiam contigisset intra annum bis vel pluries beneficium vacare; quare neque Annatarum debitum transfibat ad successorem. En ipsa Concordati verba: Placet similiter nobis quod circa provisionem diêtæ sedis ordinandam modus annatarum hoc modo currat. De Ecclesiis cathedralibus omnibus & monasteriis, virorum duntaxat, vacantibus, & vacaturis, solvantur de fructibus primi anni à die vacationis, summa pecuniarum in libris Cam. apost. taxata, quæ communia servitia nuncupantur, & si qua excessive taxata sint, quod providetur specialiter, in gravatis regionibus secundum qualitatem, rerum, temporum & regionum, ne nimium pragraventur, ad quod petentibus dabimus commissionem in partibus, quod diligenter inquirant & relaxent. Taxæ autem prædictæ pro media parte infra annum à die habita possessionis pacifica totius vel majoris partis, solvantur, & pro alia media parte infra annum sequentem, & si infra annum bis vel pluries vacaverint, semel tantum solvantur: nec debitum huiusmodi in successorem in ecclesia vel monasterio transfeat. De ceteris vero dignitatibus, personatibus, officiis, & beneficiis secularibus ac regularibus quibuscunque, quæ auctoritate diêtæ sedis conferentur, vel de quibus providebitur (præter quam vigore gratiarum expectativarum, aut causa permutationis) solvantur annatæ seu medii fructus juxta taxam solitam à tempore possessionis intra annum, & debitum huiusmodi, similiter in successorem in beneficio non transfeat. Sed de beneficiis quæ valorem viginti quatuor florenorum auri de camera non excedunt, nihil solvatur: duretque hæc observantia deinceps, nisi eam similiter in futuro Concilio de ipsius nationis consensu contingat immutari. Vel primi anni integros fructus, vel dimidiam partem solvit Pontifici, qui beneficium Ecclesiasticum obtinuit, pro annatâ. Azorius, Instit. Moral. part. ii. lib. vii. cap. xii. adducit Cofmam, Auctorem Glossæ, in Pragmat. Sanctionem, tit. de Annatis; & Duarenum lib. vi. de Sacris Ecclesiæ Ministeriis, & Iohannem Andreæm, in c. inter cætera, de officio Ordinarii, variis argumentis usum Annatarum improbantes, quod sint contra totius juris divini, & Canonici constitutiones & leges. Martinus Meyer Cancellarius Moguntinus, in epist. ad Æneam Sylvium gratulatoria adepti Cardinalatus a. cIɔ cccclvii. dum dolet in ista tempora Sylvii Cardinalatum incidisse, quando frequentes (ajebat) afferuntur de Romano Pontifice querelæ ; de annatis inter alia addit : Annatæ sive medii fructus, absque ulla dilatione temporis exiguntur, & plus etiam quam debeatur, extorqueri palam est. Quæ gravamina, adversus responsionem Æneæ Sylvii, postea confirmavit pro Martino illo Moguntino, Iacobus Wymphelingius Selestadiensis, a. cIɔ lo xv. in Replica, de Germanica Nationis & Imperii gravaminibus contra sedem & curiam Romanam. Atque ita plurimi semper Annatis illis obloquuti merito fuere, & restitere, multaque ob rationes.
